The player's wave and the compare window's mark the peaks over that level red at their edges (2022's measure, `/lab/take/wave`; a take cut before 2007, its flat tops in amber). **+dB**, beside the player's volume and in the compare window's bar (one setting, kept), plays each take that much louder, its own measure, through 1700's gain and limiter (the compare window has a graph of its own: a gain a version, one limiter that stands aside while +dB is off); the file stays as it is. The graph is made only after a hand has touched the page, since one made before stays suspended and the take plays silent. Blind, the compare window's button says +dB without a number. **The debug journal** (2054; Viktor 03.11.2026: «В Движке добавляем вкладку Debugging… ничего не отсылается никуда, кроме как по решению пользователя… Анонимизация абсолютная… Сторож на приватные данные пользователя… "Скачать лог", "Отправить лог"»; 04.11: «Гони»). Engine → Debugging, off unless chosen (`yue2.debug`); while it is on, a DEBUG mark in the bar opens it. The page (`heresy-debug.js`, the first of our scripts, so its watch is up early) keeps in IndexedDB, for a day and sixty thousand events at most: clicks, right-clicks, double-clicks, drags and drops by the element's id and data names (never its words), keys pressed as commands (never what is typed: in a field only Escape, Tab, F-keys and Ctrl/Alt letters), the rooms and the windows put over the page, each request (fetch and XHR: method, path, status, time; no query, no body; a GET answered well once a minute with how many came between), the page's errors, rejections and console errors; *With a detailed pointer trail* adds the pointer five times a second. Download and Send go through the lab (`lab/debugbundle.py`, `POST /debug/bundle`): the page's journal with the Studio's and the lab's journals of the same hours and the machine (version, system, cards), scrubbed: every prompt field cut out wherever it stands (style, lyrics, title, abc, tokens, note…), a line with a section tag, the home folder, the user's and the machine's names, addresses, mails, keys and tokens, every query's values; takes' names, titles and workspaces' names turned into marks of the journal's own salt (`take#1a2b3c`; titles looked for only where their longest word stands, as whole words: a day's journal in 2 to 15 s instead of 29). The guard reads it once more and the page says what it found; Download (`GET /debug/download`) and Send (`POST /debug/send`, a note of 500 characters) wait for a yes. Send posts the ZIP to the receiver on the card (`https://ruachstudio.igr.bible/debug/upload`, `RUACH_DEBUG_RECEIVER` for a fork) and shows the ticket; a test page (`?scope=`) never sends. The receiver's public copy with its README is `extras/debug-receiver/`. The suite's section (four checks) and a real journal of the Forge, scrubbed and read: nothing found.

**The Librarian to the end** (2058; Viktor 03.11.2026, his list «Карточки в Библиотекаре», «Дерево пространств», «Плейлист», and 04.11.2026: «Как мне узнать, где проба 1e53bb? Прикрути поиск в библиотекаре по ID проб и будет нам счастье»). What the audit of 04.11 found still open after 2046–2050, closed. **Search by ID**: a search that looks like a take's ID (six digits in a row, as the time «180155» of a folder's name, or a blind take's tail of six hex characters «1e53bb»; letters, digits and dashes only) looks through every take wherever it lives (every workspace and none, hidden, archived, frozen), whatever place is open and whatever is ticked; the heading says *Search by ID: the whole library*, each card found lists where it lives (its workspaces, 🗄 archived, ❄ frozen; *Not in a workspace*; *Hidden*), and a click there opens that place with the take flashed in sight, the eye turned on when it is hidden or disliked; the search's tip says it. **The eye** is named *Show the hidden and the disliked*, and a disliked take it brings back is dimmed as a hidden one (`is-dis-hidden`, .65). **ⓘ**: one plan a take, imported first (its cot «off» was counted as Direct), then an instrumental (the catalog's new `instrumental`: a style that begins with «Instrumental», as the Creator's switch writes it, or lyrics with no word to sing; a request without lyrics says nothing), then Full, Direct, Melody only; «N shown, M hidden» counts the disliked too while the Engine keeps them out of the lists, said apart («2 hidden (1 by hand, 1 disliked)»). **The strip** of pins and the checked is gone when there are neither (Viktor: «Только если нет пинов и нет селекции — не показываем»). **Show the hidden again** is one helper now: a workspace's ⋯ (2046), an archived one's, a frozen one's (a take frozen with its workspace stays hidden: the lab refuses it, so the item is muted and says why), and a ⋯ (or a right click) on *All Workspaces*, *Not in a workspace* and *Hidden* while they hold hidden takes. **Archived** and its workspaces count shown/all as the tree does. **The playlist**: ☰ in the bar of the checked opens First, Last, Random, the albums and New album… (the take menu's choice, in a small overlay closed by a click away or Esc); a whole workspace goes into an album as one item, as into the root (`@ws:NAME`; its ⋯ › Add to playlist, whole › an album, asked, or a new album made with it); an album's tile shows its ⋯ (rename, *Cover from…*, delete); *Cover from…* picks which of its takes' covers is the album's, square, *Automatic* the mosaic of its first covers as before; a playlist card dragged onto an album's tile goes into that album; the tags filter by the same whole parts they count («rock» no longer finds «punk rock»), and their overlay closes by a click away and Esc; *Playlist* in the column counts the root's whole list, whatever album or tag is open (his «Корень Плейлиста видит все треки»). The lab: the catalog row's `instrumental`; an album holds `@ws:NAME` (album-create, -add, -remove, -order; a workspace's rename carries it; the catalog lists it while the workspace is here); `album-cover` {album, take} ("" for Automatic; a take not in the library refused); `lab/test_library_2058.py` (12). **The lab's two debts: one look at the cards for many asks, a Writer left behind taken over** (2060; Viktor 04.11.2026: «И твои трёхсуточного бдения долги тоже, плиз»). The audit's #19: `/lab/gpus` timed out while the page loaded, since every ask ran `gpus_state()` in its own request thread with no cache, on both routes: the cards (nvidia-smi), the guard's snapshot (nvidia-smi twice more), `studio_now()` (systemctl) and the runs' cards. Measured on the Forge with its cards idle: ten calls one after another 0.196–0.220 s each, ten at once 0.39–0.57 s each (0.58 s for the ten), each nvidia-smi 65–109 ms and systemctl 15–22 ms; under a training's load nvidia-smi answers in seconds (`writer_llm._biggest` says so since 1811), and the page's load asks from several places at once (Engine → GPUs, the check before a synthesis, the Trainer, the live graphs' labels). Now the probe is `gpus_now()` and `gpus_state()` shares its look for 2 s, one refresh at a time: the asks that come while a look runs wait for it and take its answer, so a burst costs one probe; the answer adds `probed` (when the look ended) and `age_s` to the fields its callers read; the POST that saves the roles looks again at once (`fresh=True`). C10 of the 02.11 audit: `writer_llm.ensure()` used a Writer server an earlier lab left (it answered `/health`) without recording it, so the 10-minute unload, the guard's reclaim and Unload never touched it and `/llm/status` said `running: false` while it answered. Now such a server is taken over: looked for at the lab's start and every 30 s while the lab runs none, and at the first question; its pid is the port's owner (the listening socket's inode in `/proc/net/tcp`, then the `llama-server` whose descriptors hold it), its quant from its `-m`, its card from its `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (the processor with `-ngl 0`). `_alive()` follows its pid while that pid is still the writer, and the idle unload, the guard's reclaim, Unload and a quant chosen anew end it as they end the lab's own (SIGTERM, 20 s, then SIGKILL, its pid checked before each); `/llm/status` says it runs, on its card, with `adopted: true`, and Engine → Writer's pill says in its tip that an earlier lab left it. A server another running lab started (its parent a living `lab.py`) stays that lab's: used, never stopped from here, its lab's pid in `elsewhere`. Under systemd (KillMode control-group, the unit's default) the writer ends with its lab, so the Forge never had one left behind. Dry run on a scratch copy (`dry2060_lab.py`: the patched code, a fake `llama-server` on a free port, left by a fake lab that ended): 25 checks passed. Ten asks at once cost one probe of a stub 0.2 s, an ask past 2 s and one with `fresh=True` a new one, and a caller cannot change the next answer; the left server was taken over 0.2 s after the import (its pid, compact, GPU 1, `adopted: true`, its 6600 MB offered to the guard), ended by the guard's reclaim, by Unload, by a quant chosen anew and by the idle round (29 s after its 10 minutes were set as passed), and said so in the Studio's log; one on the processor (`-ngl 0`) was read as such; one a fake lab still ran stayed that lab's (`elsewhere`, Unload left it) and was taken over once that lab ended. No fake was left behind. Files: lab `apply2060_lab.py`, page `fix2060.py`, `i18n2060.py` (1 sentence ×11), `suite2060.py` (three checks, both copies), `guide2060.py` (two paragraphs ×12), and the live look `claude-2060-look.mjs` (every write held).

**The Bank Builder's loops over the vibrato, and a drone that holds** (2061; Viktor 04.11.2026: «И твои трёхсуточного бдения долги тоже, плиз»; the audit's #20: a C4 with a 30-cent vibrato found no loop, and a narrow bank's drone died after a breath). The Bank Builder: a note that wavers is looped over whole periods of its vibrato. `vibrato_of` reads the period from the note's pitch track (YIN at the analysis rate, 22 050 Hz: at 48 kHz its dip runs past its eight steps and a C4 reads 33 cents sharp, in 9-cent steps), as the sine between 3 and 9 Hz that best fits the cents with their drift taken out (from the envelope when under half of it is pitched); `loop_over_periods` looks for an end a whole number of periods after a start in the first period (a tenth of one either way), where the 40 ms around the seam correlate 0.85 or more, the level is within 1.5 dB and the pitch within 10 cents, the longest such loop first; the seam is crossfaded in the sample itself (40 ms, as the .sfz's loop_crossfade). A body of 0.25 s is enough there; a note that holds still keeps the plain match, which also stays the way when no whole-period loop is found. Measured: a synthetic C4 of 0.91 s with a 30-cent, 5.5 Hz vibrato had no loop and now loops over one period (0.183 s), the pitch step at the seam 5.3 cents against 6.8 inside the note; of the duduk sample bank's ten notes of 0.9 s or more, 7 looped and now 9 (a B3 of 1.45 s and a C4 of 0.91 s, the seam's pitch step within the note's own), and the bank built again in /tmp loops 7 of its 8 samples (5 before). The Layer: a bed or a drone strikes each key on its own; `lasts_of` strikes it ten times through the bank with sfizz (its round robins in turn) and measures how long each strike sounds before its sample ends (12 dB under its body, the sound gone after it), and the key is struck again 0.3 s before that (the banks' release), a looped one every 8 s as before. On the duduk sample bank as built on 02.11, a drone on C was silent 19.8 s of a minute (gaps up to 6.6 s) and on B 48.5 s; with 2061 not at all, with 19 and 64 strikes instead of 16 (2061b gave the silence back to its samples under 1.5 s, next entry). The Trainer's card of a built bank says «5 of 8 samples loop; as a bed or a drone, the others are struck again before they end» (the lab counts them from bank.json); a bank of calls says nothing of it. CPU only. Files: lab `apply2061_lab.py`, page `fix2061.py`, `i18n2061.py` (1 string ×11), `suite2061.py`, `guide2061.py` (×12), `claude-2061-look.mjs`.

**The Bank Builder drone's re-audit: a probe outvoted, a pluck left alone** (2061b; Viktor 04.11.2026: «И твои трёхсуточного бдения долги тоже, плиз»; the re-audit of 2061). `lasts_of`: sfizz_render now and then cuts a probe's play short (about 0.18 s at the probe's 22 050 Hz), and where a key's lengths have no period that one strike's length went to every strike of the key (the re-audit: 6 runs of 16 on the duduk sample bank; the dry run: 5 runs of 8 on its B3, which gave 0.18 s to both its round robins, an hour after none of 16; 2061b's 8 runs all right): the bank is probed twice and the probes vote strike by strike (`_voted`): where they agree, the strike is kept as heard (a round robin short by itself, a short call beside a long one, is no cut; nor, the vote's blind spot, a play cut short at the same strike in both probes); where they disagree, a length under half the key's median over both probes (a strike heard through left out of it) is a play cut short and dropped, and the strike takes the median of what is left of it (heard through in one probe and ending in the other, its end, since a strike made early never leaves a gap; every length dropped, the key's median). A strike of B3 cut 0.18 s in on purpose (the first probe's audio silenced after it): 2061 took 0.18 s into a pattern of eight it read for the key, 2061b answers as uncut, 0.84 s and 1.92 s. `held`: a key is never struck again sooner than 2 s after its last strike (RESTRIKE_S; CelloEnsPizz C3, 0.48 s, was struck 240 times a minute, now 8), and a sample shorter than 1.5 s (SHORT_S: a pluck, a pizzicato) keeps the cadence of before 2061, every 8 s. Measured, a minute each: CelloEnsPizz C3 is silent 51.1 s between its 8 strikes; on the duduk sample bank as built on 02.11, whose C4 sounds 1.34 s in its first round robin and B3 0.84 s in its first, the drone on C is silent 19.8 s again (16 strikes; 2061: none, 19 strikes) and on B 42.7 s (20; 2061: none, 64), as before 2061, the drone on A# (all looped) not at all. A built bank's card says «… the others are struck again as they end, at least 2 s apart (one under 1.5 s, every 8 s)», the guide's sentence and the CHANGELOG the same. CPU only. Files: lab `apply2061b_lab.py` (its dry run `dry2061b_lab.py`, all the kitchens on a scratch copy `dry2061b.sh`), page `fix2061b.py`, `i18n2061b.py` (1 string ×11, replaced in place), `suite2061b.py` (2061's section amended), `guide2061b.py` (×12), `docs2061b.py`, `claude-2061b-look.mjs`.

**The Librarian to the end, audited again** (2058b; the re-audit of 04.11.2026, and Viktor 03.11.2026: «На счётчике … если есть скрытые … дробное отображение типа `189/208`»). Five things 2058 left. **The bar's ☰ in a new order** (2064; Viktor 04.11.2026: «Строку "Экспорт в DAW" к хуям. Эта команда дублируется у нас в контекстном меню. **One Studio at a time** (2081; Viktor 05.11.2026: «впиши в код Сторожа… глобально, как для браузера, так и для PWA, чтобы обрубал новые/дублирующие вкладки Студии и PWA, учитывая то, что в неё можно постучаться как на порту 7777, так и на 7443. Амэн? Нам хаос не нужен, и потенциальная порча json файлов пользователя.»). The page over http on :7777 and over https on :7443 are two origins, which share no BroadcastChannel and no Web Lock, so the guard lives in the lab: `lab/lease.py`, a single writer's lease for each settings scope, kept in the lab's memory (a page opened with `?scope=` has its own, so a check never blocks Viktor's window nor his window a check). `heresy-lease.js` (after `heresy-dialog.js`): each page makes an id as it loads and claims the lease (`POST /lab/lease`, `{op: claim|beat|take|release, id, hidden, kind, port}`), keeps it with a beat every 10 s (at once when hidden or shown; the lease lapses after 30 s without one, 150 s for a hidden page, which Chrome lets beat once a minute) and gives it back on `pagehide`; a lease request waits up to 20 s, and one the lab did not answer is asked again in 3 s (2081b: the live lab answers in 0.8 to 1.8 s while a page comes up, and the first cut of 5 s took a busy lab for one not answering). Held by another live page (asked twice, 1.5 s apart, for a reload's own release on its way), the page's own dialog asks: *Work here* takes the lease, and the other page learns it at its next beat or write and turns read-only, a plain banner under the bar with its own *Work here*, which takes the lease back through a reload so nothing the other window changed is written over; *Close this one* calls `window.close()`, and where the browser keeps the tab a calm *You can close this tab* screen stands. While the lease is asked for, a write of the page waits; held, a write to the lab goes named (`?inst=ID`, `ID@SCOPE`); not held, it is answered in the page with a 409 that says why (reads and listening pass, `OPEN`, the same list in both); fetch, XHR (Import) and `sendBeacon` alike, and `heresy-settings.js` sends nothing from a read-only page. The lab refuses with a 409 every POST that names a page instance not holding its scope's lease (a lease lapsed and taken by nobody goes to the writer: a lab restarted under a working page), and that 409 turns a page that believed itself the writer read-only at once; a request naming no instance (an API client, a page from before) is untouched. The engine forwards only the query to the lab, so its own few writes (Compute's Save, Security, a take's card and its delete, a generation) are held in the page, not by the lab. Not by itself in a test browser (the checks call `window.ruachLease.start()`); a lab without `/lease` leaves the page as it was. The suite's mock serves `/lab/lease` with the lab's own `lease.py` and refuses as the lab does. i18n: 8 phrases ×11. Guide ×12: a row of *When Something Goes Wrong*. Suite: one section (this page and a second one in a frame: the second asked and waiting to write, Work here, the first read-only with its banner and its writes answered 409 by the lab and then in the page, an unnamed write untouched, Work here back; a third closed to its calm screen; a scoped page never blocked; Russian). `lab/test_lease.py`. Kitchens in `MISC/claude-arc/k2081/`.

**The user's data backed up** (2083; Viktor 05.11.2026: «в Движок умолчанием пропиши ежесуточный/ежечасовой бекап json данных пользователя, с предвыбранной ротацией gz бекапов. Kept in every snapshot, the JSON the Studio writes as its user's state: `user/settings.json`, `presets.json`, `collection.json` (the Librarian: workspaces and their sections, notes, ratings, pins, locks, frozen and protected takes, the playlist, albums, reactions, the LoRA notes, the workspaces' notes), `playback.json`, `refiner_profiles.json`, `writer.json`, `access.json`, `audio.json`, `analog_loop.json`, `c2pa.json`, `gpus.json`, `user/vocab/*.json`, `user/videos/*.json`, `user/plugins/*/plugin.json`, `writer/*.json` (the Writer's documents) and `writer-versions/*.json`; in the daily and Back up now snapshots each take's `outputs/*/meta.json` too (3 513 cards, 1.8 MB here); never a take's `request.json` (82 MB here, written once with the take), the caches, the queues or a test page's files. A snapshot is one `.json.gz` in `user/backups/` (`hourly-…`, `daily-…`, `now-…`), written whole (a `.part`, fsync, a rename) and read back before an older one of its kind goes; hourly keeps 24 and daily 30, both on by default (`user/backups/config.json`), Back up now its last 10. A file that does not parse is never stored: it is put back first from the newest snapshot that holds it whole, and that copy goes in. Put back only over a file truly broken (it does not parse, read twice 0.5 s apart): at the lab's start, when the lab's read of the settings, the presets or the Librarian fails, or at a snapshot's read; the broken file is copied to `user/backups/broken/NAME.STAMP`, the snapshot's copy takes its place in one rename, and a notice waits until the page says once (the window that writes, 6 s after its start) which file and from when; no button puts a snapshot back. The writers first: the settings, the presets, the places' record, the Librarian, the player's marks, the Refiner's setups, the writer's choice, the audio interfaces, the Content Credentials (written in place until now), the cards' roles, the Writer's documents and their import, the Creator's versions and the Videographer's plans now write a `.part`, fsync it and rename it; `access.json` and a take's `meta.json` are the engine's own (C++), left as they are. Engine → Folders and Security → *Backups of your data* (`heresy-backups.js`): every hour and every day on or off, how many to keep, the folder, *Back up now*, the last snapshot's time and size (`GET /lab/backups`; `POST /lab/backups`, `/backups/now`, `/backups/seen`, a test page's changing nothing). i18n: 15 phrases ×11. **A deeper backbone, switched to in the same engine** (2090; Viktor 05.11.2026: «…обязательно в Студию, в публичный код»). The probe of 05.11 found the engine dead (the kernel's `yue-server segfault at 38`, in the music half's attention) when it switched to a backbone with more layers than the one it started with: `pipeline_configure` shapes the music cache by the boot backbone's config and `qw3lm_kv_alloc` makes its views for those layers alone, while both switch paths, a job's own backbone (`backbone_for`, HERESY 1661) and the Engine's choice (`settings_apply`), unloaded the models and kept the cache, so the deeper backbone read a NULL view past the cache's last layer. `kv_reshape_for()` (`tools/yue-server.cpp`), on either path after `store_unload_idle`, reads the new backbone's config, keeps the Engine's context, frees the cache and gives it the new shape, so the next run allocates it for this backbone. Behind it stands `qw3lm_kv_fits()` (`src/qwen3-lm.h`): `qw3lm_forward` and `qw3lm_forward_batch` refuse a model deeper than its cache (or with other heads) before they read it, and now return false; `yue2_prefill`, `yue2_generate` and the pipeline's two forwards pass it up, and `g_qw3lm_error` reaches the job's error through `pipeline_generate`'s `last_error`, so the job says why instead of the engine dying. Tested on a spare engine with the original 3B and a deeper backbone that sings bit-identical to it: the binary before the fix died on the first switch (`segfault at 38`, as on 05.11); the new one sang 3B, the deeper one and 3B again by the job's backbone, then the deeper one and 3B by the Engine's choice, in one process, the cache shaped anew at every switch, five takes of one PCM. The guard alone, without a card (`k2090_guard_test.cpp`): a deeper model over a shallower cache refused by both forwards with its reason, a shallower one over a deeper cache let through. Kitchen: `MISC/claude-arc/k2090/` (`k2090_switch.py`, `switch-test.json`).

**A soft start against the decoder's first-millisecond tick** (2091; Viktor 05.11.2026: «после декодера убирать его сразу же… плавный вход… по умолчанию»). The codec ceiling heard it on the shofar and measured it on every decoder: a tick in the first millisecond of a decode, the edge of the decoder's window. Measured in the engine itself the ceiling's way (above 3 kHz, zero phase, the first millisecond's peak), on 18 of its pieces (their first 5 s through the standard encoder, then each decoder): 33 of the 54 decodes stood more than 6 dB over their original's first millisecond (the shofar −19.35 dBFS Standard, −23.77 Legacy, −20.35 Blend against −40.16; a Torah chant −18.1 against −68.5). `audio_soft_start()` (`tools/yue-server.cpp`) lays a raised cosine of 10 ms (1324's fade-in curve) over the start of every take the engine decodes, by default: the songs of a run (`run_job`) and another decoder's take (`decode_job`, HERESY 1168), before the user's own fades and the MP3's normalizing; `--soft-start <ms>` sets it, 0 turns it off. Why 10 ms: with the engine's own curve on the raw decodes, 1 ms took the tick away from 11 of the 33, 2 ms from 16, 5 ms from 30, 8 ms and longer from all 33, and 10 is the shortest of the 10–20 asked, with 2 ms to spare. It leaves an opening hit −12.5 dB over its first 5 ms, −1.6 dB over its first 20 ms and −0.3 dB over its first 100 ms; Viktor's thought of 250 ms would take −43 dB over the first 20 ms and −16 dB over the first 100 ms, the downbeat itself. The engine's own takes: the shofar −81.76, −82.65, −82.03 dBFS in the first millisecond, a solo guitar −88.50, −89.84, −89.23, each the simulation to the sample and past 30 ms the raw decode to the bit; two 3B takes from their kept latents, −58.76 and −60.35 before, −104.1 and −112.77 after. Only at a take's own start: every decode the engine makes a take from begins there (a regenerated part, Replace a section, Sing once more and the window are rendered with the whole song, kept codes and new together, as one stream); the bare `/vae` decode is the codec's own and stays untouched. Kitchen: `MISC/claude-arc/k2090/` (`k2090_cpu.py`, `k2090_fade_pick.py`, `fade-pick.json`, `cpu-recheck-10ms.json`).

**Writes counted, timed, sent again, and said when lost** (2099; the same journal: in the stalls on the road the writes took 38 to 121 s, and POST /lab/collection at 13:58:02 (50.2 s) and POST /lab/settings at 21:45:23 at home (32.1 s) fell without an error and without a retry). Each write the page sends to the Studio or its lab (not its own heartbeats, the lease and `perf/beat`, nor what waits for a long answer by its nature: a writer's reply, an upload, an export) is counted until it is answered; while one has waited 1.5 s a chip in the bar before DEBUG shows the count with a cloud and its arrow (`HeresyIcons.ui("upload")`), its tip naming each one with its seconds, amber once one went again. The quick ones (`/lab/collection`, `settings`, `presets`, `playback`, `lyrics`, `writer`, `writer/versions`, `refiner/profiles`, the Artist's note, star and protection, `derived/mark`, `backups/seen`, `llm/hosts`, `video/save`, `orchestra/map`, the audio gateway and balance, `train/protect`) carry a write id (`?wid=`, 18 hex) and wait 20 s (60 on a far line, `HeresyNet.far`); no answer, or the engine's 502, or 503, 504, and they go again, twice more, 2 and 6 s apart, with the same id, said once in a toast («No answer yet (no answer in 20 s): «…» is sent again»); after the third the write says it is lost («Not saved: «…». The Studio did not answer after 3 tries (…); your change is not on its disk. Try again when the line is back.») and its promise is rejected with those words, never resolved empty; a write that is no quick one and dies on the way says so too («No answer from the Studio for «…»: it may not have been done. Look before you do it again.»). The lab answers a write id it has seen with its first answer, byte for byte, and does it once (`lab/write_once.py`: kept ten minutes, two thousand at most; a second sending that comes while the first is still at work waits for it up to a minute, then is answered 503; the engine passes the query and not the headers, hence `?wid=`), so a workspace is never made twice nor a playlist shuffled twice by a retry. The settings' sync sends one at a time (a push every 4 s piled up behind a stalled one).

**The lease on a bad line** (2100; the same journal: between 16:00 and 20:00, 213 of 758 lease requests fell, 201 of them cut by the page's own 20 s timer and only 12 by «Failed to fetch»; at 16:45:26, right after an Alt, 19 lease POSTs went out in 3.6 s, and 113 of 215 failures were sent again within 5 ms). `heresy-lease.js`: one lease request in flight (a beat asked while one is on its way is that one); the page's comings and goings beat at most once in 1.5 s and never during a beat or a miss's pause, through one listener, the module guarded against a second run; a beat waits 8 s and a claim 15 s, each cut by a timer whose reason says it is the lease's own («the lease's own timer: no answer to its beat in 8 s»), so the journal no longer reads it as a stuck request; a beat without an answer is a miss, the page stays the writer, the next beat comes after 10, 20, 40, then 60 s, and the misses go to the lab in the next beat (`missed`), which keeps a holder on a bad line 90 s instead of 30 (`lab/lease.py` `TTL_SLOW`), so more than one missed beat goes before another window may take the lease; the page turns read-only when two answers in a row say another window holds the lease (at once when it was taken there by Create here); a chain of timeouts instead of an interval. Each change goes to the page as `ruach-lease` {state, why} and to the debug journal with its reason, and the lab's log says every change of holder (who, by what, how long the one before had been silent).

**The line stuck, said quietly** (2101; the same journal: the Studio and its lab fell silent in the same millisecond, 16:37:57.266 and .267, and came back together at 16:42:31–33, while at home the engine went on generating through a stall: the path or the door, not the lab nor the engine). When three or more requests to the Studio and its lab have waited 8 s (24 on a far line) and nothing has been answered in that time, in a tab in sight, the page shows a broken link in the bar (`HeresyIcons.ui("unlink")`, its tip: how many, how long, that the Studio itself may be well) and the log's line time says «· the line is stuck» in amber; the background asks (the cards' graphs, the activity, the hardware, the props, the batch, the backups, the Writer's state…) wait until something answers, one each (a second of the same path is refused at once with «Held: …»); the first answer takes the sign away and lets the held ones go. The journal keeps the stuck and clear moments.

**The guard reads with eyes of its own** (2119; Viktor 03.11.2026: «Анонимизация абсолютная… Сторож на приватные данные пользователя»; the review of 2104). 2104 had the guard look for addresses with the scrubber's own pattern, so what the scrubber left the guard could not see: an address with «peer/» before it stayed whole and the guard said nothing. `lab/debugbundle.py`: the guard has a pattern of its own, wider: four dotted groups of one to three digits wherever they stand (after a word and a slash, glued to a letter or an underscore, with leading zeros), each up to 255, not inside a longer dotted token (a card's «94.02.42.00.A0»); only a browser's version (one of the browsers' own names and a slash before it, «Chrome/142.0.0.0») and this machine (127.*, 0.0.0.0) are let by. The scrubber is as it was; what it leaves, the guard now names before anything leaves. Over the Forge's own journals of the last day, scrubbed (1 751 lines of the Studio, 47 446 of the lab), it names nothing. `test_debug_scrub_2104.py` gets five checks, and writes this network's addresses as a prefix and two numbers, so make-release's scan for them finds none in it.

**One toast a failure** (2120; the review of 2099, 06.11.2026: «No answer from the Studio for …» or «Not saved … (HTTP 503)» stood beside the caller's own toast of the same failure, «The chain did not start: …»). `heresy-link.js`: what it has to say of a write lost (no answer, or the last try answered 502, 503 or 504) waits a moment (400 ms) for the caller's own toast of it; when one comes, these words stand under it as its second line (nothing more when the caller's toast says them already, as it does when it shows the rejection's own words), and only when no caller says it are they a toast of their own. Its own toasts are marked, never taken for a caller's. The suite's journal section waits that moment for the toasts it reads; a new section shows each case.

**A write held by Create here is no write lost** (2121; the review of 2099 and 2100, 06.11.2026). A quick write made while the lease asks *Create here* waits for the answer in `heresy-lease.js`; its own 20 s ran meanwhile, so a question left up a minute ended in «Not saved… The Studio did not answer after 3 tries» with nothing wrong on the line. Its time starts once the question is answered now (the lease says `asking()` and gives `settled()`, the promise of the answer), and the debug journal notes the write held. The suite holds a write behind the question 4.5 s on 1.2 s waits: nothing sent, no try counted, nothing said; after *Create here* it goes once and is answered.

**The player's title only gains room** (2122; Viktor 22.10.2026 on the mirror of 1741: «Зеркальная точность»; the review of 2107). With its likes made 444 px wide for a probe, the title at 1920, 2560 and 3840 keeps 90 px with the two marks as icons and the right side whole, where steps 3 to 7 took the four parts and then the title; at 1660 the speed still goes for a part over another, and nothing past it. The 2107 sweep runs from 700 px (700, 768, 800, 852 added), each step there shown needed, the Trainer's and the Videographer's own «wants a wider screen» answered as it comes.

**The Refiner keeps the way in hand across an F5** (2127; Viktor 06.11.2026: «полнейший Аудит Студии на скрытые баги, уязвимости и проёбы по UIX»; the audit's high finding in the Refiner): after every F5 the canvas lost the way in hand. **The Studio's doors after the full audit: the relay, the frames, the keys** (2138; Viktor 06.11.2026: «полнейший Аудит Студии на скрытые баги, уязвимости и проёбы по UIX»). The relay of 2005 gave a chat server's own type back, so `/lab/relay?to=…` opened by a link, a bookmark or a messenger ran that server's page or script in the Studio's origin, and it checked a name at one address while urllib looked it up again to connect (a name that answers twice, DNS rebinding, was checked here and asked there). `lab/relay.py` now connects to the very address it checked, the name kept for Host and TLS, and answers JSON alone (what is not JSON is said as JSON with its first words); `relayed()` adds nosniff and `sandbox; default-src 'none'`, the engine's `/lab/` proxies pass both, and the relay opened as a page, a frame or a script is refused by the engine (`relay_opened`, `//relay` too) and by the lab's gate. A page of another site could put the Studio in a frame and lay its clicks over the Studio's buttons: every answer of the engine now says `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` plus Pinokio's own page (its app view frames the Studio from `http://localhost:42000`; the laptop's Pinokio keeps the Studio's storage under that top page) and the origins `RUACH_FRAME_ANCESTORS` names (INSTALL.md, docs/API.md), and a navigation to `/` from another site passes as a document or as a frame of a listed page, an embed or an object never; the https door passes the headers as they are. The move to https (1985) handed the whole storage over plain http, a Remembered OpenRouter or Civitai key too, against 1012's promise that the key goes only to openrouter.ai: `heresy-settings.js` now names its secrets in one list (`HeresySettings.secrets`), the hand-over keeps them back, and the https page says once which keys stayed and where to put them in again. A take's title with a line break no longer begins a header of its own in the lab's downloads (`byte_ranges.py`, as the engine's `download_header`). Checked by `lab/test_relay.py`, `test_origin_gate.py`, `test_byte_ranges.py`, `test_tls_door_headers.py`, the engine's gates compiled alone, the hand-over in node:vm, the suite's 2138 section and curl against the built engine (sec-live-check.sh, 22 checks).

**Every file of the page kept, each under the key of its own content** (2139; Viktor 06.11.2026, about 06:00, reading the briefing over his remote connection: «Вот очередная загрузка шрифтов без кеширования - это неприятно на удалённом соединении. Да и все assets загружать с кешированием, но в каждом иметь ключ `?675tg9` релиз тега»). The engine's `/lab` relay dropped the lab's Cache-Control, so the page's fonts (15 on a load, 2.48 MB) came again at every reload; the page went `no-store`, 17 MB (5.3 MB gzipped) each time; the covers, the manifest and its icon had no validator at all; a remote reload moved about 10.8 MB. **The key** is not the release tag he wrote but each file's own content: the first ten hex of its SHA-256, written `?v=KEY`. It changes exactly when that file changes, so a release that leaves a font alone does not make every remote browser fetch it again, and a file changed between two releases gets its new key at once (a release tag would send all 83 fonts again at every release, and keep a file changed between releases under its old tag); the release itself is shown in Engine → About, the page's build id beside it. build.sh writes the keys into the stylesheets' `url()` (the 137 faces of 83 fonts), the page's manifest and icon links and the manifest's icons (the manifest written beside the page), and hands the piano roll's 124 sounds theirs in `window.RUACH_BUILD` with the build's id and the release from VERSION (`RuachAsset(url)` adds them); `/arts` says each cover by its key. The engine (`tools/asset-cache.h`) and the lab (`byte_ranges.py`) keep a file a year, immutable, only when the URL's key is its own, and answer anything else `no-cache` with an ETag and a 304 when unchanged: no key, an old page's key or a made-up one never holds the wrong content for a year. Who may keep what (NETWORK-EDGE §3.2): the Studio's own files (the fonts, the sounds, the app's icons and manifest) `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; the covers, the user's own, `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, kept by the browser alone; the page `private, no-cache` with a weak ETag of its size and time, a 304 that never reads the file, a new build shown on the next reload as before (1130). The guide and the vocabularies stay unkeyed, `no-cache` with a 304, since they are written between builds. The relay passes the lab's cache headers and its 304 and sends the browser's validators on; four answers of the lab that now reach the browser were not named by their content and would have shown a replaced file old, the adapter's picture (10 min), the DAW's impulse (a day), the spectrogram's slice (an hour) and a look's preview (10 min): each is `no-cache` with its validator now. A page back from the browser's back/forward memory loads again, as Back did before; the worker's offline page asks `/health`, not the page. Measured on the live Studio, headless (`?scope=claude`, muted): a cold load 10.97 MB on the wire in 150 requests, a reload 1.33 MB in 68, the page a 304 and every font and cover from the cache (what is left are the Librarian's lists); with all 1031 covers drawn, a cold load 205.4 MB and a reload 1.47 MB, and the lab was asked for no cover again. Checked by `lab/test_asset_cache.py` (53 checks), the engine's header against sha256sum, build.sh's keys on a copy of the tree, `cache-live-check.sh` (16) and `cache-suite.mjs` (13) on the live Studio.

**The card on its own domain, ruachstudio.art** (2140; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Меняй адрес в коде и готов замены в карточки репозиториев. Старый URL станет редиректом 301.»; «2.0.6 подожди тогда срезать»). The visiting card moves from ruachstudio.igr.bible to https://ruachstudio.art, served from the same folder on the web server, and the old address answers 301 to the same path and query (Viktor's nginx, his hands). `site/build.py`: `SITE` is the new address, so the 13 hreflang alternates, the x-default, the canonical and the og:image of the 13 pages follow it; each page also says its own `og:url` now, and the build writes `sitemap.xml` (the 13 pages with their alternates, and the vocabulary's page) and `robots.txt` (its Sitemap line; /debug/ is no page). The Studio: F1 › About links the new address and shows it; the debug journal's *Send* names the new receiver (the key changed with its words in the 11 catalogs, and in the pending Hebrew one with its chunk and `keys.json`, which still rebuilds byte for byte); the lab's default receiver (`lab/debugbundle.py`; `RUACH_DEBUG_RECEIVER` still overrides it) is https://ruachstudio.art/debug/upload. The lab posts with Python's urllib, which turns a 301 into a GET without the body and follows no 307 or 308, so the old address keeps /debug/ served ahead of its 301 for the labs before this one; no released version posts there (the receiver came with 2054, after 2.0.5), and 2.0.0–2.0.5 reach the card only by About's link, a browser's GET that follows the 301. The new address also in the README, `site/README.md`, `docs/FW-VOCABULARY.md` and `docs/TW-VOCABULARY.md` (and `render_md.py`, which writes them), `extras/debug-receiver/` (its README; `nginx-debug.conf` says the block goes in both server blocks), the Starter Sets' draft card, the promo end-cards and recorder, the HF cards' generators and the suite's check of the *Send* dialog. `MISC/claude-arc/he-card/deploy-he-card.sh` checks the new address (pinned to 24.109.223.46 as before, robots.txt and sitemap.xml among its files); `sums`, and `old` alone, check that the old one answers 301 to the same path on the new one and serves /debug/ straight. Drafts, nothing published: the four HF cards with the address (`MISC/claude-arc/domain/hf/`; `upload.sh` uploads them only once https://ruachstudio.art answers 200 with a valid certificate), GitHub's homepage field (`github-homepage.sh`; the description untouched) and `NGINX-NOTES.md` for Viktor. History stays: the CHANGELOG of released versions, the older entries here and the dated reports keep the old address, and the 301 answers for them.

**The card's jokes, withdrawn** (2141, withdrawn; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Они, хоть и в своих цитатных оформлениях, но идут потоком. Пройдись по сайту и глянь, что поместить с autowrap прямо в тексты, даже в цитатные блоки, — всё равно будет смотреться, а что сдвинуть вверх или вниз и тоже красивее врезать»). The visiting card's eleven Heretical Tandem notes came, in its lower half, every 550–850 px on the Russian page at 1024 px: a stream of identical boxes. Four boxes stay, far apart: the octave in the rooms, the Russian dataset in the ring, the 358 GB in the downloads, the two limits in the credits. The other seven are no box but a run of the text they laugh at, after its last sentence and in its flow: the agent and the tokens at the end of the declaration's quote, the honest guard after «A guard against garbage», the four kilohertz at the end of figure 1's caption, the themes after the themes line of «The screen», the forty-eighth take after «heard blind before it ships», the small s after the licence of the name «Ruach Studio» (its wavy underline kept), and the division of labour as a quiet line of its own at the top of the footer. Each is a `<small class="tandem-in">` with a `<span class="tj">` per language: a pepper, the speakers' names in the accent, the rest in a softer slanted gold (upright in Japanese, Chinese and Hebrew; never under 14 px). Every telling keeps its words; only the layout changed (a dialogue set as «—» turns, the narration and the end line joined). build.py shows the page's own telling of these too, and ends a text's translation unit before its joke (a joke that is not the last thing in its element stops the build), so the text keeps its translation: all 13 pages build with nothing missing. **A card out of memory leaves its tracks out of the step** (1812; 28.10.2026: a three-card training stopped a fifth of an epoch in when one card met a ~9.7 k-token AR input, the style head, a sheet near the 6 000-token cut and the song's first 3 000 tokens, with gradient checkpointing already on; the trainer raised and torchrun ended every card). **Two flakes of the suite fixed at their cause** (2195; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Абсолютно все мелочи закрываем»; H19, wf_3220cc55 review:audit) There were two of them. The first was 2094's «the −6 line drawn faint», which sometimes read 255 against 40–120. It sampled the line at x 2, and the compare box's playhead is a 2 px opaque bar drawn over the time played. Whenever the audio had gone about 2 px in before the sample, the playhead stood over x 2 and the sample read its full 255. In a calm run the playhead was already at x 57–58 when the sample was taken, so it does move. The section now reads row 1 of the wave, which holds no bars, finds the columns where something full-height is drawn, and samples a gap between bars away from them, near three quarters along. The tolerance was right, so it is unchanged. A probe that brought the playhead to x 1–2 read 255 at the old spot and 77 at the new one. The second flake was «Promise was collected» in 1742's «blurred pastel blots». Its `finally` switched rooms and returned at once. It now waits 300 ms after the switch, as the suite's other room-switching sections do. The old section stopped the run with «Promise was collected» in 2 of 3 slices where it ran three times among its neighbours (1741 before, 1743 after). The new one passed all three such slices (20 of 20 each time) and six repetitions alone. The 2094 section passed six times alone and three times among 2093 and 2095, before and after the change.

**The https door refuses a request it could read apart from the Studio** (2222; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Абсолютно все мелочи закрываем»; the smalls' checklist, the audit of 06.11.2026 §2.5 and §7 item 17). `lab/tls_door.py` read a request's framing more loosely than the engine behind it: it took the last of two Transfer-Encoding headers where cpp-httplib takes the first, stripped a space before a header's colon, let a folded line, a bare LF, a second Content-Length of another value, Transfer-Encoding beside Content-Length, «gzip, chunked», a negative or «0x» chunk size and a chunk longer than its size pass on. Where two readers of one stream disagree on where a body ends, the bytes one takes for a body the other takes for a request, and such a request never passes the door's own reading, its X-Ruach-Peer included (2011). Today's engine (cpp-httplib 0.44) refuses each of these by itself, so nothing was open through it; the door no longer leans on that. It now checks every header line (a token name, a colon right after it, no CR, LF or NUL in the value), allows one Transfer-Encoding and only «chunked», never with Content-Length, a Content-Length only as one number, a chunk size only in hex and a chunk's end only as CRLF; anything else is answered 400 «The Studio's https door refused this request: …», as RFC 9112 asks, after the answers the Studio still owes on that connection (the door half-closes its side to the engine and lets them finish), and nothing of it passes. A chunk found bad mid-body leaves the Studio a body cut short at what the sizes said, and the 400 is the visitor's last answer. Proof: `lab/test_tls_door_framing.py`, a stand-in engine that reads its body by the first Transfer-Encoding as cpp-httplib does: at lab 1c45102 eleven of its thirteen checks fail (the request hidden behind «chunked, identity» reached the stand-in with the visitor's own X-Ruach-Peer: 127.0.0.1), on the branch all thirteen pass; `test_tls_door_headers.py`, `test_https_door.py` and `test_origin_gate.py` pass as before.

**FlashSR's archive yields plain files inside its folder alone** (2223; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Абсолютно все мелочи закрываем»; the smalls' checklist, the audit of 06.11.2026 §2.5). `lab/upbundle_job.py` unpacked FlashSR's code from its author's archive refusing only a «..» in a name: a symbolic link came out as a link, a file named after it was written wherever it pointed, and an absolute path was honoured (Python 3.12's tarfile trusts an archive fully unless told otherwise). The archive is pinned by its revision and comes over https, so this was a fence missing, not a door open. Now `unpack()` takes only plain files and folders whose path stays inside the folder, through tarfile's own «data» filter as well; links of both kinds, devices, absolute paths and «..» are left out and named on the job's stderr, never dropped unsaid. Proof: `lab/test_upbundle_tar.py` on an archive holding each of them beside two good files (four checks pass); the probe `door-probes/upbundle-old-loop.py` runs the loop as it stood on the same archive and shows two links made inside the folder and two files written outside it.

**A plugin's MIDI script fenced for real** (2224; Viktor 06.11.2026: «Абсолютно все мелочи закрываем»; the smalls' checklist, the audit of 06.11.2026 §2.5 and §6). `heresy-midi.js` ran a plugin's MIDI script in a worker after `self.fetch = undefined`, which hid only the worker's own property: `WorkerGlobalScope.prototype.fetch` and `importScripts` were still there, at the Studio's own origin, and read the Studio as the page does, while `heresy/root/docs/PLUGINS.md:122` promised «no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket or importScripts». The worker is now made from a `data:` address, so it runs at no origin of the Studio's: whatever it would ask is a stranger's request, which the engine and the lab refuse (Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site) and whose answer the browser does not let it read; and fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, importScripts, indexedDB, caches, Worker, SharedWorker, BroadcastChannel and WebTransport are taken from every object of its prototype chain. PLUGINS.md says so, and says what it is not: a module from a site on the internet that answers anyone can still be imported, so the worker stays a fence for the page, not against the plugin's author. Proof: a suite section with a script that looks for those names up the whole chain and reads `/lab/plugins` with what it finds: on the page as it stood it found fetch and importScripts and read 22 bytes at the Studio's origin; on the branch it finds none and runs at origin «null»; the MIDI section of 1169 · 1589 (a plugin's action and words through its worker) passes unchanged.

**The engine on ggml 0.29.0, our mask patch moved over** (2240; Viktor 07.11.2026: «Переключай ggml»; the VAE-RS port's ggml step).
