**A plan written by two threads at once stays whole, and no update is lost** (2308; found by Claude 10.11.2026 when SeedVR2 finished Buratino's 40 shots on three cards within a minute: the plan came back unreadable, «'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd1 in position 140172», and eight upscales went aside). Every writer of a plan used the same `NAME.json.part`, so two collectors finishing together interleaved their bytes into one file and moved it into place; and the lab's collector thread and every status call collected the same finished jobs at the same time. Now each write has a temp file of its own (pid and thread), the three setters the background threads call (a shot's picture, its H3 video, its upscale) read, change and write the plan under one lock, and the H3 and SeedVR2 collectors run one at a time (a second one leaves the work to the first). The broken plan was rebuilt from its 14:02 copy plus the 40 H3 and 40 SeedVR2 job records through the room's own setters; nothing was lost.

**The Reader's ear writes Greek again, hears it by its sound, and judges a word of another script by its consonants** (2311; Viktor 10.11.2026: «Не транслитерируй ничего для Чтеца. Пусть всё идёт на своих глифах. Не придумывай костыль, плиз.» Claude's card text, read by the Reader in five languages on the morning of 10.11 with its Greek and Hebrew transliterated, was read again that night exactly as the card writes it: Αἵρεσις, «וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת», אֵשׁ and רוּחַ in their own letters. The word guard had flagged 46 words in the Greek reading, and they were looked at one by one. Most were not Drama's at all. The ear (reader_hear.py, HERESY 2295) suppresses Whisper's digits when a text has none, and it chose the tokens by their byte-level names: there the bytes 0xB2, 0xB3 and 0xB9 are «²», «³», «¹», digits to `isdigit()`, so 1930 tokens went with them, among them every one that writes β, γ, ι in Greek and в, г, й in Russian and Ukrainian. Whisper, unable to write γ, wrote «λόgos», «πληκτρολοぎου», «έغραψε», and «ξεθάυουμε» for want of β. Now the suppressed tokens are those whose text holds an ASCII digit: 426. The Greek card's pieces heard again with the ear as it was: 17 words flagged (with the fold below), letters 8.2 % off; with the fixed ear: 0 words, 1.3 %. The rest was the fold: Whisper writes Greek by ear (η, υ, ει, οι for one [i]; αι for [e]; ω for [o]: «λέη» for «λέει», «είνε» for «είναι»), and the names in Latin letters (Viktor, SUNO, Ruach, credits) came back in Greek ones. The score now hears Greek by its sound (`_el_sound`: digraphs, iotacism, a Latin word read as a Greek reader says it, a letter of a script no reading has dropped), a Latin name in a Hebrew text by its Hebrew consonants («ל-SUNO» heard «לסונו», «Anthropic» heard «אנתרופיק»), and a word of a third script (Αἵρεσις in Russian, וְרוּחַ in Greek) by its consonants in Latin (`_skeleton`), and leaves such a word out of the letters' score on both sides (`score_near`): a word read right in other letters is no edit, a word dropped still counts. A hyphen between letters parts words («Γραμμή-Γραμμή»). Whisper's sign-off on a piece's trailing quiet («Продолжение следует», «Thanks for watching» and their kin in eleven languages, only when put in after the piece's last word) is no word put in: the Russian card's piece 5 was read three times for it. Drama 3's four middle tiers were measured again on a whole free RTX 3090, each with its own session options: mid-q4 RTF 0.89 (was 1.34), mid-q6 1.15 (1.74), ram-q4 1.46 (1.75), ram-q6 1.52 (2.46), CER 0 on «Утро в Кузне» but for mid-q6: its take with cuda_perf put in the very «пошидим» Viktor marked down in the blind quants on 09.11 (the same seed without cuda_perf, RTF 1.21, reads clean; cuda_perf samples on the card, so one seed proves little: Viktor's call); mid-q6 peaks at 15.2 GB, so it asks 15400 MB of the card (was 14500). Heard in the Russian reading, for Viktor's ear: רוּחַ came out as «руха» (the patach under a final ח is said before it: «руах»), «וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת» as «веруха элохим мрахефет», Αἵρεσις as «Айресис».)

**TTS Voice Upscaler: Resemble Enhance in the Refiner, for the Reader's takes only; its credit and Fish Audio's in the Engine's About** (2312; Viktor 09.11.2026: «TTS Voice Upscaler… Resemble Enhance под капот… строго в мире Чтеца: denoise убирает шум и музыку под речью, enhance апскейлит говорящий голос, пресеты»; approved with all the node's defaults, float32 only: «модель и так мелкая, здесь не дешманить»; the credits in About for Resemble Enhance and for Drama 3 with «Built with Fish Audio». Resemble Enhance (MIT, Resemble AI, its last commit 8e97814 of 03.12.2024) is vendored as `lab/reenhancert/`, its inference only: no training, deepspeed, omegaconf, matplotlib, pandas or tqdm; the stage-2 hyperparameters written in; NumPy 2's `fsolve` fixed; the debug quantiles of `IRMAE.encode` left out; its LICENSE and a NOTICE beside it (and alias-free-torch's Apache-2.0). The weights are read from `models/reader/resemble-enhance/enhancer_stage2.safetensors`, converted from the released checkpoint with its own fp16 tensors (sha256 96e272bd…), and computed in float32; its denoiser matches the upstream's output at 67 dB SNR. The step `tts_upscale` (the Studio's own plugin, group mend, read by `.venv-read`: no Reader's interpreter, no step) has four modes, Clean (the denoiser alone), Upscale (midpoint, 64 steps, tau 0.5, lambd 0.1: the Space with its box off), Restore (lambd 0.9: the box on, for a noisy source) and Draft (32 steps); «only the top» (on by default for Upscale and Draft) keeps the take sample for sample below the cut (12 kHz by default) and takes the drawn band above it with vupscale's crossover, so the generative enhancer never touches the engine's words and stresses; a mix, and steps, solver and temperature for the expert. Out at the take's own rate when it is 44.1 kHz or more, else at 44.1 kHz, its length the take's; 30 s chunks with 9.5 GB free on the card, 10 s with 4.5, else the processor (said in the log and the summary). A step may now be bound to a realm (`"realm": "reader"` in plugin.json, passed to the page): the Refiner keeps it out of the list and the canvas until the take in hand is of that realm (`/derived` says the take's realm), and the lab refuses it on any other take (live: «TTS Voice Upscaler: only for the Reader's takes», 400). The step and its runtime stay home with the Reader (make-release leaves them out, check-no-pro.sh ⑤ stops a tree that carries them). Where the Reader is, About → Models in the Studio names «Narration: Fish Audio Drama 3» (Fish Audio Community License · Built with Fish Audio) and «Speech upscale: Resemble Enhance, by Resemble AI» (MIT). Checks: test_reader_upscale.py (the step bound and hidden without its interpreter; Clean and Draft on the processor: rate, length, the take kept below the cut), tools/claude-check-tvu.mjs on the live page 8/8. A blind duel against AP-BWE (24 → 48 kHz, MIT) and LavaSR (the Vocos-based BWE of arXiv 2603.07285, Apache-2.0) waits for Viktor's ear in «🧪 Чтец · TTS Voice Upscaler вслепую»; CodecFlow (arXiv 2603.02022) has no code or weights published.)

**The DAW's bar grid from the take's own tempo, meter and sections, one grid the Videographer can cut on: bars and beats on the ruler and through the lanes, cuts, copies, the loop and a click clinging to them** (2313; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Сетка тактов и привязка к долям: вырезки, копии, петля»; §2.6 «Резы по битам и секциям — от той же сетки тактов, что в DAW»). Measured first, on seven of Viktor's takes (10.11.2026, librosa's beats against the score's Q:): a song as YuE2 sings it does not keep its score's tempo to the beat. The beats heard ran 0.1 to 1.3 % off the score (Буратино v9.3.6, written at 85, sang at 86.1: 5.6 s ahead by the end of its seven minutes; Синт-поп №14 alone kept 120 to 0.2 %), and a take without Q: (read at 120) sang at 132 or 143. So the grid at the score's tempo from 0 s, the one the REAPER and DAWproject exports and the Videographer's cuts lay today (dawproject.tempo_meter), is bars off by the end of most songs. `lab/bargrid.py` hears the take's own sound once (librosa's tracker on its onset strength, the score's or the style's tempo its prior; a pulse heard twice as fast as the score's halved, half as fast doubled) and lays the bars on the phase where the music itself changes (takechanges, the changes the player snaps the sections to), where the downbeats sound strongest and, with a score, near the song's start; with a score its bars are the score's own (a bar of 3/4 among 4/4 kept), each laid on the heard beats, so they follow the take's drift. Kept beside the take (`bargrid.json`, as takechanges keeps changes.json) for its audio's time and size; what the hand sets (twice or half the tempo, where a bar begins, beats a bar) kept in it and the grid derived again from the beats kept, nothing heard again. GET and POST `/lab/daw/grid` (its own lock, never behind a mix's render). On the page, `heresy-bars.js` (`window.RuachBars`): the grid asked once a take, the lines a view shows at its zoom (bars, beats, halves and quarters of a beat as there is room), the nearest line, a time's bar and beat and back. The DAW draws the bars numbered and the beats ticked on its ruler (32 px with the grid, 46 with the sections) and faint through the lanes; the selection's edges, a carried stretch's start or end, the loop drawn on the ruler and a click cling to the grid's lines within 6 px as they cling to the sections (1972); G turns the grid off and on, Alt held lets go. Its button's right-click and the ruler's: a bar begins here, twice or half the tempo, beats a bar, as heard, hear it again; the grid said in the page's words. For the Videographer: `bargrid.grid(take_dir, audio, req, changes)` is the same grid, kept in the same file; its `_rhythm` can take it in one line (not done here: its code is another night's). How it was proven: `lab/test_daw_grid_2313.py`, 34 checks (the level, the phase from the changes and the downbeats, the score's bars and chords on drifting beats, a click track at 100 bpm with accented downbeats heard end to end by librosa, the hand's settings kept and derived without hearing, refusals); the page through a headless probe of the built page on the test lab with four copied takes (the grid at 120.24 bpm for №14, snapping at the whole song's zoom, G, the menu, «a bar begins here», twice and as heard), 0 page errors.

**A chord and key lane in the DAW, from the take's own score** (2314; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Полоса аккордов и тональности внутри нашего DAW. Пока аккорды уходят только наружу»). The take's score (its request's, else the one the transcriber wrote from its sound) read by the lab's own checker (abc_tools); its chord symbols and keys laid on the bar grid's heard beats (2313), a chord held over bars one span: the same grid the bars stand on, so a chord stays on its bar when the take drifts from the score's tempo. On the page a lane of 20 px under the ruler, inside the ruler's sticky row: the chords as blocks with their names, the one sounding lit as it plays, a key change marked; the key at its left. A click goes to a chord, a double-click loops it; its tip says the chord, the bar and beat, the key. Shown while the take has chords and the lane is wanted (the grid's menu turns it off and on). Proven on Синт-поп №14 (34 chords, Em): `test_daw_grid_2313.py` (the chords on drifting beats, a chord over two bars one span, the key) and the probe (the lane 20 px, the key Em at its left, its chords drawn; a click and a double-click).

**The DAW's reference from any take or someone else's song, at equal loudness** (2315; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Эталон из любого дубля или чужой песни на равной громкости»; 02.11 it stood next in line). Ref (1755) heard only the set's own source. A right-click on it now chooses: the sound as it came (as before), a sound of this take's tree (its mixes, its masters, its prints: every branch's file but stems and lanes), another take of the Library (found by its title), or a song of your own sent to Forge (kept in `user/references/` as FLAC, 48 kHz, two sides, by the first twelve hex of its bytes' SHA-256: the same file twice is one reference), and your references kept for every take, each to be forgotten. Whichever it is, it is measured block by block as the source is (K-weighted 100 ms blocks, gated as the page gates the mix's) and played from the same second as the mix, as loud as the mix over what has played; the choice kept for the take and set in this browser; the button underlined while it is not the source. Lab: GET `/daw/refs`, `/daw/ref/loudness`, `/daw/ref/chunk`; POST `/daw/ref` (the file as the body), `/daw/ref/delete`; a reference never names a file outside a take's folder or the references. Proven: `lab/test_daw_refs_2315.py`, 21 checks (the specs refused that reach outside, an MP3 kept as FLAC 48 kHz two sides and deduplicated, a file ffmpeg cannot read refused with nothing left, the blocks gated to Plenio's integrated loudness, stretches at the file's own rate, past its end silence); the probe: another take as the reference (6 s played from 0:30: matched, its stretches streamed), a song of mine sent, measured, forgotten.

**Bounce in place: a bus, a VCA's lanes or one lane into a lane of its own in one action, the mix unchanged** (2316; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Bounce in place: шина или группа полос в новую полосу одним действием», so the layer and the Refiner take what is already mixed). A lane's menu, Bounce in place: its bus, its VCA, or the lane alone with its devices. Forge renders what those lanes put into the master as the mix stands (`daw_mix.bounce`): each one's strip as heard (its mute, solo and VCAs as the mix has them), through its bus's chain when the whole bus is among them, with their share of the room and the delay (the returns are linear: what these strips send makes this much of them); the job writes it as a lane of its own (a branch of kind "bounce" whose file says its track, read by the set as an added strip, 1929's way); above full scale it is written lower and its lane's fader raised as much. When it lands its members are muted (a soloed member's solo goes to it) and it plays at 0 dB, so the master hears the same sum, its chain and the song's fade after it as before; one undo gives the members back and mutes the new lane. A bus shared with lanes left out is refused (its compressor hears them all), and the menu greys it with the reason. The tree names the kind (Bounce in place). Lab: POST `/daw/bounce` {name, set, mix, versions, members, title}; Stop as a mix's. Proven: `lab/test_daw_bounce_2316.py`, 13 checks: a bus with its compressor, a VCA with a keyed compressor, one lane with a cut and an S-shaped level, the room with its pre-delay and cut and the delay with its loop, the master's limiter and fade: the mix rendered before and after the bounce is the same to 1e-9 in each case, the soloed case and the one above full scale too; the job's lane read by the set. The probe bounced a bus of two lanes on the test lab: its lane in the set, its members muted, undo and redo.

**Audition from the click point: one lane alone from where it is pressed, while it is held** (2317; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Прослушка (Audition) с места щелчка», Bitwig 6's audition). Alt pressed on a lane's wave plays that lane alone from there, as it is set (its devices, its line, its cuts), the reference out of the way; let go, the mix as it was: playing on if it played, else stopped with the playhead back where it stood. Nothing of the mix changes: no solo, no undo step, nothing kept. With a lane's line in hand (A on) Alt bends a segment instead (2318); Alt still lets a drag go free of the grid once it has begun. Proven by the probe: Alt pressed on Bass at 30 %: Bass alone, playing from 0:53, its lane lit; let go: stopped, the mix's value byte for byte as before.

**The lines' shapes: a segment's bend, hold or S, the spread of a stretch, an LFO on the bar grid** (2318; Viktor's unified plan of 08.11.2026, §2.4, the DAW list of 02.11 (from the DAW research of 01–02.11: Bitwig 6, REAPER 7.84, Live 12.3, Logic 12); his «агенты как не в себя гонят… все долги и планы» of 10.11.2026: «Формы автоматизации: кривизна, „держать“, „размах“, LFO»). A point of any line (the level, pan, width, the sends) may say how the line goes on to the next: a bend (−1 … 1; Alt+drag on the segment with the line in hand, its middle following the pointer), hold (it stays, and steps 1 ms before the next point) or an S (half a cosine); a double-click on a segment makes it straight again; its menu (a right-click on the line off its points): straight, the change late or early, hold, S-curve, an LFO, the spread, the line taken off. The spread draws the points of a stretch in or out about their middle (0 % flat, 200 % twice as wide), heard as it moves. The LFO (sine, triangle, square, saw up and down; from the top or the bottom; its depth and centre line) is laid as the line's own points, two a cycle, each segment shaped (the sine a row of S's, the square held), its cycle a length on the bar grid (a sixteenth to four bars, following the take's beats) or, without a grid, Hz; at most 2000 points a line, said before. It acts on the lane's selection, else the loop, else the section at the playhead; the selection's menu offers it on the level too. A shaped segment is laid out as the points a straight line goes through (one every 20 ms, 2 to 24 a segment) by the page (expandPts) and by the render (`daw_mix.expand`) alike, so the line heard, drawn and rendered is one; ruach.mix/1 takes [t, value, shape]. The fades' box and these boxes now open over a floating console (z-index 80, the menus still over them). Proven: `lab/test_daw_shapes_2318.py`, 21 checks (the shapes refused that it does not know, hold one point 1 ms before the next, the S's middle half way, a bend late and early, a held level rendered as a step, and the page's expandPts run under node against expand() on 60 random lines: the same points to 1e-9); the probe: the shapes kept in the value, a line's menu, an LFO of four bars (8 points from the top, an S each) and a square a beat (32 points, held), the selection's menu laying it.

**A song or a reading that would wait long behind the Videographer, the Artist or a training asks first: wait, or off the queue** (2319; Viktor 10.11.2026: «если все ресурсы заняты, не просто ставить в очередь… в очереди будет стоять генерация либо в музыканте, либо в чтеце, допустим, будет очередь там час, ё-моё, это ненормально… ставить такого сторожа и реально уведомлять, что извиняй, но, блин, это придётся целый час ждать. Либо ждём и блокируем последующие очереди по музыке и ТТС, либо просто снимаем с очереди этот трек»). `lab/waitguard.py` answers `GET /lab/waitguard?kind=music|reader` with how long such a job would wait now and behind what, each long work by its own progress: a MiniMax H3 worker by its shot's step and the shots queued on its card at that card's own seconds of work per second of video (33 s by default for a draft), a SeedVR2 upscale by the frames it has made, a plan's keyframes by the shots drawn, an Artist run by its pictures and steps, the lab's other jobs by their own expected time, a training by the trainer's ETA; a time it cannot know is said as not known, never as 0. A reading that needs a card waits for the first of the works on the cards it may read on (cards full with none of the Studio's works on them: another program, said as not known); one that needs the lab's heavy turn waits for what holds it, a batch that takes it again (the keyframes) and the jobs queued ahead of it (`turn` now says which job holds it). A song waits only behind work on the Studio's own card: on the Forge the Studio sings on the Intel card, so there only the Reader ever asks. The page (`heresy-waitguard.js`) asks before `/synth` and `/reader/say`; above Engine → Defaults' new «Ask before music or speech waits longer than» (5, 10, 15, 30, 60 min or never; 10 by default, `yue2.waitAsk`, reset with the defaults) it shows the wait, each work with its card and its time left, and two answers: «Wait (about N min; music and speech wait behind it)» or «Take it off the queue» (never sent; a song's other versions follow). Waiting, a song is held in the page until the card is free (asked every 15 s, its hold kept alive, sent when nothing holds the card) and a reading is queued at once, its hold bound to its run until the run begins; while either waits, a later song or reading that would wait too is not queued: the question names the waiting one and offers «Take “…” off the queue» (a queued Reader run is cancelled with it) or «Keep it waiting». A lab without the route (404) or not answering stops nothing. The strings in all twelve catalogs. Checked: `lab/test_waitguard.py`, 31 checks; the routes on this lab code in a process of its own (port 41879): hold, seen, release with cancel, a 400 for another kind; `tools/claude-check-waitguard.mjs` on the live page (?scope=claude, muted, the lab's answers stubbed in the page so nothing is queued): 23 passed in English and Russian, 0 page errors. The running lab takes it at its next restart (pending: other agents' work was on the cards).

**/health sees the Videographer's workers and the Artist's kept painters; a lab restart waits for them** (2320; 10.11.2026: a restart of the lab at `"jobs": {}` killed three MiniMax H3 workers mid-shot, since systemd stops the unit's whole cgroup and `/health` knew only the lab's own job table). `/health`'s jobs now carry each MiniMax H3 worker (`h3 gpuN`: running while it loads or makes a shot, queued with shots waiting, idle when it only holds its card), each SeedVR2 upscale of the Videographer (`seedvr2 …`, running), a plan's keyframes (`frames …`) and each kept painter of the Artist not painting (`painter gpuN`, idle), and a `workers` list says this lab lists them. The reload waiter (`systemd/reload-when-idle.sh lab`) waits while any is running or queued (an idle worker or painter holds only loaded weights: a restart costs their load, never a shot), and with a lab from before this (no `workers`) asks `pgrep` for `h3_worker.py`, `upscale_job.py` and `artist_job.py` itself. `lab_busy()` (the move of the user's folders, the updater) counts them too, and the updater restarts the lab through its reload (`reload-or-restart`) instead of a bare restart after a build of minutes. `build.sh` restarts only `ruach-studio`, whose cgroup holds none of the lab's workers: nothing to change there. Checked: `lab/test_waitguard.py` (a busy, an idle and a dead H3 worker, a SeedVR2 job, keyframes); the waiter's check against the running (older) lab with a stand-in `h3_worker.py` process: busy; without it: idle.

**The Videographer's key frames painted on every card of the lab's jobs at once, each card's painter loaded once for its share** (2322; Viktor 10.11.2026: «держать художника загруженным… максимальная оптимизация ресурсов, а не просто на одной карте все херачить и перезагружать модели»). Buratino's forty shots were forty Artist runs one after another, each its own painter process: Qwen-Image 2.1 loaded forty times on one card (about 105 s a hero shot, of which 2512's polish 30 s), GPU2 never used, 100 minutes. Now `frames_job` draws a plan as two batch runs (`artist.draw_batch`, `artist_qwen.batch`): first every hero shot by 2.1 from the hero's picture, then 2512 over those at 0.35 together with the shots from words alone, one painter with the same realism adapters for both, so it loads once a card. Each run is dealt over every card of the jobs with room (1354), a card's share painted by one process with its prompts read before the painter comes (2512 kept between runs as 1370's); each picture is set into its shot as it comes. The room's line says the step, the pictures done of the step and the cards. Measured the night of 10.11 on Buratino's first ten shots (0:00–1:16, seven with the hero) on three cards: 686 s (2.1 on all three 437 s, 2512 238 s) against 1241 s for the same shots run by run; 2.1 paints about 140 s a picture when three cards go at once (its parts on the card in turn), 2512 15 s from its reference, 39 s from words.

**MiniMax H3 shots spread over every free card of the lab's jobs, and no card idles while another has shots waiting** (2323; Viktor 10.11.2026: «у меня в настройках в студии же выставлено на лабы 3 видеокарты… Нужно выдавать видеографу все ресурсы в реальности»). The shots were dealt to the cards' queues when asked for, and a card that came free later (GPU0 behind the Artist's forty runs) got only what was asked after it: Buratino's forty took GPU1 81 and GPU2 78 minutes of work, GPU0 29. Now an idle H3 worker takes the oldest waiting shot of the longest other queue of its kind (`h3_worker.steal`, a rename: the owner either took it first or never sees it, the record's card rewritten), and the lab's collector starts a worker on a free card of the jobs while shots wait beyond one for each worker there is (`h3_shots.spread`, asked through `more_gpus` only then). An upscale asked while idle workers keep their cards for their ten minutes sends them away first (`h3_shots.release_idle`; the night test's «Upscale all» right after the last shot found no card). The ten shots on three cards: 21.0 minutes, of it 5.7 loading the three workers at once, the cards 811, 908 and 907 s busy (one shot taken from another card's queue); the same ten shots took 23.0 minutes on two cards before.

**SeedVR2 7B sharp in fp8 as a choice beside 7B sharp and 3B; measured what a shot costs** (2324; Viktor 10.11.2026: «Вопрос, на скольких шагах ты его херачишь. Может быть, это too much»). SeedVR2 paints in one step; a shot's time is the VAE (its decode in tiles about half of it, the encode a fifth) and the 7B's DiT, whose 16 blocks streamed from RAM. Measured on two Buratino shots (107 and 141 frames) on one 3090: 7B sharp fp16 with 16 blocks swapped 433 s a shot, 7B sharp fp8 400 s, 3B 365 s, 7B sharp fp8 at 720p 220 s (16.3 GB; the clip scales it to its size); tiles of 1536 run out of the card, tiles of 1088 gain nothing. The default stays 7B sharp fp16; the shot's 🎬 menu has 7B sharp fp8 and its 720p too, and Upscale all asks which of the four. The side-by-side for his eye: heresy/MISC/claude-arc/night-2026-11-10/videographer/.

**The Writer's look names one place, and a shot's prompt keeps one scene** (2325; 10.11.2026: Buratino's setting was three places one after another, «Carlo's tiny cupboard workshop… then a dark theatrical stage… and finally a muddy backstage swamp», and 2512 painted shots as split screens of them). The Writer is asked for ONE place in the look's setting, a shot that happens elsewhere saying where in its own words, and for one moment in one place in each shot. A setting written before that lists places one after another («then», «finally», «;») is left out of the shots' picture and video prompts, the shot's own words saying where; the picture prompt ends «One single still frame of a music video: one scene, one place, no text.»

**The clip's render says where it is and the time left** (2326; Viktor 10.11.2026: the render of Buratino showed no progress). The shots' share of the progress is 45 % when the last pass encodes the whole clip again (words, a look, the film, a scaling), else 90 %; the last pass's progress is read from ffmpeg as it writes (`-progress pipe:1`) against the song's length. The room says «the clip: 63 % · the final pass 2:31 / 5:37 · about 5:52 left», or the shot it is at, or the dissolves.

**A finished clip has its card in the Library, right after its song** (2327; Viktor 10.11.2026: Buratino's clip had no card beside its song). The catalog carries each take's finished clips (`videographer.clips_index`, drafts left out); the Library puts a card for each after the take's own, so it stands in the song's realm and workspace: ▶ plays the clip over the page (Esc closes it), 🎥 opens the take in the Videographer.

**SheetSage2-Refined, the Studio's second transcriber: a switch wherever a score is transcribed and in the Trainer's sheets** (2328; Viktor 10.11.2026: «Берём его файнтюн к нам в Студию и оформляем его как альтернативный оригинальному SheetSage2… переключать в Творце/Музыканте и в Тренере при сборке датасета кнопками как VAE варианты»; «Да, именно так».)

anime-song's [SheetSage2-Refined](https://huggingface.co/anime-song/SheetSage2-Refined) (weights CC BY-NC 4.0, code MIT) keeps SheetSage2's ear (MERT-v2-FullSong with its LoRA) and retrains the writer: a decoder whose vocabulary grows by 898 tokens (a chord as its bass, then root × 62 qualities with tensions; keys with nine modes), steered by small frame heads. The file is scragnog's GGUF overlay ([SheetSage2-Refined-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/scragnog/SheetSage2-Refined-GGUF), sha256 aab21b68…f11832), installed as `models/SheetSage2-Refined-F16.gguf` (155 MB).

It does not load in the old transcriber as it is: another architecture (`sheetsage2r`), other tensor names, the larger vocabulary, and a decoder trained with the bar heads' facts added to its memory, so the heads are not optional. The engine now reads the overlay itself (`src/sheetsage-refined.h`, `src/sheetsage.h`): SheetSage2's GGUF beside it gives the encoder, the layer mix and the projection (F32 first, `YUE2_SS2R_BASE` names another), the overlay the decoder; seven layer mixes come out of the encoder graph for five frame heads that run on the CPU (two bar heads whose 43 facts go into the decoder's memory, the chord, quality and key heads whose tables rescore its logits), with the prompt-aware grammar, the mode bias and the unpadded window of the reference. The heads, grammar, tables and rescoring are ported from [HOT-Step CPP](https://github.com/scragnog/HOT-Step-CPP) (MIT, Rob «scragnog»; the licence text in the header).

Measured against the MIT reference (PyTorch, model revision e36ce4f, code c9e5d7c) on the Ring's first card: on the CPU 98.3 % of the tokens other than time are the reference's, the times within 40 ms; on the Arc 93.5 %, the difference one beat the decoder wrote again at the time of the one before (a near tie in the SYCL numbers at 48 s), which the engine leaves out instead of failing the score. SheetSage2's own path is untouched: a 40-second clip transcribed by the old and the new build is byte-identical.

The labels: chord symbols in SheetSage2's own spelling (maj7, m7b5, m(maj7), a slash bass named by its degree, D#/F##), tensions in parentheses (G7(b9), Cmaj7(9)); keys with modes as ABC writes them (Ddor, G#mix; harmonic minor as minor, phrygian dominant as phrygian, the raised degree an accidental in the notes). The notation's key table learnt the mode suffixes (an unknown key ended the whole process before).

The server: `--transcriber-refined <gguf>`; `/transcribe?transcriber=refined` (and `modes=1` for keys with modes), the same as form fields; `/props` says `transcriber_refined`; the result names the transcriber that wrote it. `start.sh` passes the file when it is there.

The page: Composer → Cover or Remix → From a Recording has **Transcriber: SheetSage2 / SheetSage2-Refined**, chosen like a VAE and kept in the browser, with «Keys with their modes» under Refined; a take of the Library is transcribed with the same choice, and the status says which wrote the score. Match sections reads whichever score is in the form. The Trainer has **Transcriber** beside Mode: Refined's sheets are files of their own beside the set (`NNN_ruach.full.refined.abc`), never mixed with SheetSage2's. `megaset_sheets.py --transcriber refined` writes the megaset's sheets into `datasets/work/sheets/full-refined/` through a list tool of its own (`yue-transcribe-list-refined`); SheetSage2's store and the running training's sheets are not touched.

Found the same night, while Refined wrote no chords at all for the Ring's second card: MERT's rotary angles. anime-song's reference rounds them to bfloat16 the way SheetSage2 was trained (positions, frequencies, their products and the cos and sin; positions above 256 fall into steps of up to 32 frames), and says exact angles break SheetSage2 (beat F 0.985 to 0.447 in its measure). Our MERT turned them exactly: its inner states stood 20 to 34 % off the reference, Refined's memory 35 % off. With the rounded angles (`mert.h`, tables in place of `ggml_rope_ext`, for SheetSage2's encoder only, the audio tokenizer untouched) the states are within 4 to 7 % and the card's chords come back as the reference writes them (F, D#, Gm; 80 bars, as the score it was sung from). Refined always uses them; SheetSage2 keeps its exact angles unless `YUE2_SS2_ROPE_BF16=1` (its sheets so far were written with them: Viktor's word decides; the Ring's numbers in the night's report). A beat written again at the time of the one before, which on the Arc made SheetSage2 refuse whole scores ("beat times must be strictly increasing"), is now left out for both transcribers; SheetSage2's scores that never hit it are byte-identical.

The page read neither: `heresy-abc.js` refused `G#maj7(9)` and `K:Ddor`, so a take sung from a Refined score lost its section markers, its MIDI for REAPER, speed and arrange; the 47 spellings and the mode keys are read now. The Ring, all twenty cards from their audio (on the CPU after the Arc hung at 21:38), against the score each was sung from: chords bar by bar SheetSage2 0.81, Refined 0.82 (0.87 leaving out card 20, where Refined writes no chord at all, as its reference does); bars exactly as sung 7 against 9; meter changes 82 against 17 (the scores have 9); keys 20 and 19 of 20 (20 with modes). On the Arc, before the fix, SheetSage2 refused 15 of the 18 cards it was given. The FULL covers (three cards, three scores each) are in the workspace «🎼 SheetSage2 / Refined · FULL»; the song model read Refined's chords without a stumble.

Found on the way: the transposer moved a slash chord's root and left its bass standing (C/E up a tone became D/E, SheetSage2's chords too); the bass now moves with the root. Strings in all twelve catalogs.

**Our decoders finished for 2.0.7: true float32 on CUDA, on Hugging Face, and fetched by every install** (2329; Viktor 10.11.2026: «прикручивай основным VAE версию 1, наш VAE, чтобы он был как стандарт в студии»; 09.11.2026: «v3 статистика для нашего протокола внутреннего, не наружу»). **CUDA in true float32.** ggml sets TF32 on every cuBLAS handle and computes F32 in its mma kernels in TF32, so the RTX 3090 decoded YuE2-VAE-RS x3 only −55 to −67 dB from the kit's PyTorch reference. A ggml patch of ours, `build/ggml-patches/0002-cuda-f32-request-on-src1-no-tf32.patch`, gives ggml's own precision request its meaning on CUDA: a matrix product whose input asks for F32 (`ggml_prec_set_src(…, GGML_PREC_F32, 1)`) skips the mma kernels and runs cuBLAS with TF32 off for that call only, the handle's mode restored after it. `vae.h` asks for it on the two products of the F32 decoder (the unfolded convolutions and the transposed ones); Standard's F16 path asks nothing. Measured on GPU2 under its lock against `reference/yue2_vae_rs_reference.npz` (64 s, four tiles; the start, both seams and inside the last tile, after the WAV's turn-down past full scale): v1 −55.4…−65.5 dB before, −110.9…−114.5 after; v2 −63.9…−66.7 before, −112.9…−115.8 after; Standard the same bytes before and after (md5 d44d59a7), as on the Arc B50, where v1 stands at −113.8…−118.2 dB; the decode as fast as before. The fifth excerpt, the song's last 4096 samples, reads −44.5 dB on every backend and binary alike: the engine ends at 1920·T − 64 samples as m-a-p's decoder does, the reference at 1920·T. **On Hugging Face, private until Viktor's word:** `goldhub/YuE2-VAE-RS` holds both decoders as float32 safetensors and as the engine's GGUFs, the integration kit (`yue2_vae_rs.py`, `verify.py`, the ComfyUI node pack, the two patches, `vae_rs_gguf.py`), the licences (weights CC BY-NC 4.0 in `LICENSE`, code Apache-2.0 in `LICENSE-CODE` with `NOTICE`), the model card and the scientific document; the card's blind listening reads «by ear, results coming», and no v3 number is in the card or the document. Kitchen and upload: `MISC/claude-arc/codec/vae-rs/release/hf/` (`hf_vae_rs.py stage` checks every text file against `MISC/private-terms.txt`; it found the dataset's private name and a kitchen path in the document, both taken out). **The document** (`doc/build_doc.py` → `doc/VAE-RS-x3.html`): the v3 section, its column and rows in the loss table and every mention of it gone, sections renumbered (Release 9, Licences 10, Credits 11), §8 still fed by `doc/data/blind.json` and marked «by ear, results coming», §9.1 names the repository and the GGUFs, §9.2 the engine's float32 on CUDA; checked headless at 1920 light and dark, 390 and 2560, no overflow (the page has no script). **The download lists:** `fetch-models.sh` brings RS x3 v1 with every song's least (beside Standard, which still encodes) and v2 in the pack «extras»; an update brings v1 once, the pack «newdefault» that `tools/models_plan.py --update` wants though it is not here (checked with a mocked file list: an empty install gets v1 and not v2, this one gets nothing); `heresy/fetch-heresy.sh`'s part «extras» is our two decoders instead of Legacy and Blend; `lab/weights.py` says «our decoders», 1.6 GB, and its restart hint follows any fetched `models/` line; README's What It Downloads and its Models table name our decoders (the install 41.6 / 34.9 GB). `heresy/hf-revisions.txt` pins the repo at 1d9dec46. Until the repo is public the lists say «the pinned file list could not be read (offline?)» for it and plan nothing of it; the card on the web server (`root/site/i18n/*.json`) still says «two more decoders» with the old sizes, for the 2.0.7 cut.

**Viktor's two ComfyUI workflows in the Artist: ComfyUI's way (the same seed, the same picture) and his samplers grid** (2332; Viktor 09.11.2026: «выход из ComfyUI… перенести мои два воркфлоу»; his orders protocol: «Перенос твоих двух воркфлоу»). His AIO QWEN IMAGE 2512 HERESY Draft #4 (346 nodes in 17 groups) and his Ultimate Samplers Testing (three nodes of JasonHoku's grid pack) were read node by node, and the graph ComfyUI really executed for his QWEN2_00075 was taken from that picture's own metadata: what reached the sampler, not what the widgets showed (both passes take er_sde and bong_tangent from one SamplerParameterPacker; the first pass's CFG is the 4.5 slider, beside Lightning 0.55; the second pass paints with Detailz 0.6 and Qwen Enhancer 0.7, from step 20 of 60; the upscale stack is span ×2, Nomos8kDAT ×4, Remacri ×1.5, UltraMix ×2, then 7680 on the long side and ColorMatch). `lab/artist_comfy.py` is ComfyUI's arithmetic for Qwen-Image 2512 rebuilt in the Studio: the starting noise drawn on the CPU from the seed in the latent's own shape, ER-SDE's noise on the card from the same seed, the model's sampling (Qwen-Image's flow shift 1.15, or ModelSamplingFlux with his max shift 3 and base shift 0.5 by the picture's size), every schedule as ComfyUI computes it (simple, normal, SGM uniform, beta, beta 57, KL optimal, Karras, exponential, bong tangent), the guidance as ComfyUI's without diffusers' norm rescale, Skimmed CFG's linear interpolation, the conditioning as ComfyUI's entries that each act in their share of the steps and are averaged (ConditioningZeroOut, ConditioningConcat, SeedVarianceEnhancer's two entries), a LoRA hooked to some entries only, its strength by keyframes as comfy/hooks.py steps them, the prompt read with ComfyUI's template, his abliterated Qwen2.5-VL and his Clear VAE when asked (copied into artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/encoders/ and vaes/; the VAE brought to diffusers' layout by diffusers' own converter, which gives the Studio's VAE back tensor for tensor from ComfyUI's), and the sigma given to the time embedding in float32 (diffusers rounds it to bfloat16). Measured against ComfyUI's own code on the CPU: the sigma tables, all nine schedules at 12, 16 and 60 steps, the seed variance, Skimmed CFG and his hook keyframes equal to the last bit.

Three things diffusers and transformers do their own way are done ComfyUI's way, each measured on the CPU against ComfyUI's own code equal to the bit. The adapters go into an fp8 fine-tune as ComfyUI puts them, not beside it as PEFT does: each layer's patches added to its weight in float16 (what ComfyUI computes them in on an Ampere card), the sum rounded back to fp8 by chance with the layer's own seed (the CRC-32 of its key), the hooked adapter added in float32 on top while a hooked entry is painted and rounded again with the same seed (comfy/model_patcher.py; with hooks ComfyUI loads the painter whole): Fp8Lora, 81 checks against comfy/float.py, comfy/lora.py and its key map. The painter's forward is ComfyUI's arithmetic on diffusers' own layers (its rotary table in bfloat16 from float64 angles, turned in bfloat16 with one product rounded and the second fused; its modulations and gates as fused multiply-adds; torch's fused rms_norm; its last layer's fused multiply-add): comfy_forward, equal to ComfyUI's QwenImageTransformer2DModel on two of Hyphoria's blocks at three sigmas, where diffusers' own forward stands 0.35 to 1.3 % (relative RMS) from it at one step. And the prompt is read as ComfyUI reads it: the encoder kept in its file's bfloat16 (ComfyUI's llama_detect, whatever its log says of float16) and worked in float32 with llama.py's rotary turn, causal mask and fused norms: comfy_te, equal to ComfyUI's encoder on a prompt of 32 tokens, where the Artist's float16 reading stood 0.33 % from it with two thirds of its values off in bfloat16. `comfy.merge: "peft"`, `comfy.forward: "diffusers"` and `comfy.te32: false` paint the Studio's own ways for comparison. What stays diffusers' is the VAE and its tiles.

Findings for him from the graph itself. His «MAIN CONTROL» keyframes never act: CombineHooks keeps one hook of the same LoRA node (comfy/hooks.py, HookGroup.add compares the hooks' shared reference), so only the first chain steps his character adapter (0, then 0.4 to 1 from 30 % to 50 %, 1 to 80 %, easing to 0.8). And with ModelSamplingFlux at max shift 3 the shares of the steps fall at the very top of the schedule (a quarter of 1664×928 is σ 0.9953): the seed variance acts on the first step alone, the adapter is at full strength from the second (0, 0.4, 1, 1, 0.86, 0.83, 0.81, then 0.80), and in his second pass (3328×1856) it holds 0.80 of its strength all the way. His saved Draft #4 puts InjectLatentNoise+ at 0.6 where the graph that made QWEN2_00075 had 1.0: the button follows the saved graph, the proof the picture. And today's ComfyUI (0.20.1) cannot paint his second pass with its dynamic VRAM on: it keeps 3.4 GB of its buffer beside the painter and runs out of memory at the second step on a 3090 (ComfyUI's own log, 21.84 GiB allocated); with --disable-dynamic-vram it paints it (65 s a step on a 3090, its own hooks re-laid at every keyframe). With nothing hooked (his samplers grid), the dynamic VRAM lays the adapters otherwise than the classic load: a layer's first pass with the sum unrounded in bfloat16, then rounded with the seed of the layer's name; Fp8Lora.arm_dynamic follows it, and `comfy.merge` defaults to auto: dynamic when nothing is hooked, classic under hooks, as ComfyUI chooses ("fp8" asks for the classic load).

The page: «ComfyUI's way» in the Artist's form (on or off; ComfyUI's seed up to 20 digits; the text encoder and the VAE; CFG beside Lightning; Skimmed CFG; the model's sampling; the negative as nothing, its words kept for their length, which shapes the empty negative as ComfyUI keeps it; second words; the seed variance; the hooked adapter with its strength and trigger; a second pass from a step of its schedule, its colours put back), two buttons that fill the form as his first and second pass (his own adapters stay his pick: no private name in what ships), and «To the form» of such a run brings them back. «Samplers grid»: samplers × schedules × steps × CFG × a stepped adapter's strengths × prompts, 64 pictures at most, one run, the painter loaded once a fine-tune and every prompt read once, laid out on a board in its run (samplers down, schedules across); Again draws it again from a new seed; «His grid» fills his «LoRA Weight #6». The lab: `POST /artist/draw` takes «comfy» and «grid» (lab/artist_recipes.py checks them; artist.draw_grid), `/artist/painters` says which of his encoders and VAEs are here, and a lab of before this says so on the page instead of painting the Artist's own way unsaid. Test: `lab/test_artist_comfy.py` (25 checks, no card); the CPU parities against ComfyUI's own code are in heresy/MISC/claude-arc/night-2026-11-10/artist-comfy/test/ (parity_cpu, parity_er_sde, parity_fp8, parity_forward, parity_te).

Proofs on his own pictures tonight, the cards taken in turn with the night's other rooms (heresy/MISC/claude-arc/night-2026-11-10/artist-comfy/proof/, private: his character adapter is in them). His second pass, over the same first pass (ComfyUI's own of tonight), by ComfyUI and by the Artist: the same picture, mean difference 2.0 of 255 at 3328 × 1856, PSNR 34.5 dB, 95.8 % of the pixels within 8 levels (ComfyUI itself had to be run with its dynamic VRAM off: on, it runs out of memory at the second step); 35 minutes on a 3090. With his 8K chain after it, beside his QWEN2_00075 of May: the moon, the mountains, the fire on the water, ФОСФОРИДА, the face, mean difference 18.5 of 255 at 7680 × 4284 — and ComfyUI's own second pass tonight stands as far from his May picture (18.4): today's first pass parts from May's in its details, not the port. His first pass, step by step against ComfyUI's own latents: 0.14 % apart after the first step, 0.5 % after the second, 3.2 % after the fourth against ComfyUI with its dynamic VRAM off and 7.9 % against it on — and ComfyUI against itself, the dynamic VRAM on and off, is equal to the bit for two steps and 7.7 % apart after the fourth. No switch of the run explains the first step's 0.14 % (the seed variance, Skimmed CFG, CFG, either negative entry, the hook's strength, Lightning: none lies along it); the Artist sits as near to ComfyUI as ComfyUI sits to itself, and ER-SDE at CFG 4.5 grows that into the details of the last step (the moon of ComfyUI's picture; mean difference 24.1 of 255, it was 28.3 before tonight's three arithmetics). His samplers grid (BASE fp8 at 1024², Lightning 0.8 and his character adapter 0.9 laid on the painter, nothing hooked, 3 samplers × 3 schedules): which of ComfyUI's two loads made a picture decides its composition, the adapters rounded into fp8 by chance outweighing their own change. The ER-SDE cells: ComfyUI's default (dynamic VRAM) against the Artist's dynamic way 41.3, 2.5 and 10.4 of 255 (beta 57, KL optimal, bong tangent); ComfyUI's classic load (--disable-dynamic-vram) against the Artist's classic way 18.8, 14.5 and 2.7; across the two loads 50 to 86, other compositions. **The Reader's pauses: a tag in the text cuts the piece there and stands after it to the hundredth of a second as heard; the take's editor shapes every pause, in place or in a copy that is the take's child** (2334; Viktor 08.11.2026: «теги пауз [pause:600ms] и [pause:6s] (длинная — место для музыкальной вставки)… потом сторож и полуручная доводка: режем копию и удлиняем паузы до сотой секунды; оригинальный выхлоп никогда не удаляется, всё дитя в древе дубля, как в Творце»). `lab/reader.py`: `[pause:600ms]`, `[pause:6s]`, `[pause:1.25s]` (a bare number in seconds; 0.05 to 60 s) is the Studio's own tag, never an engine's (Drama 3's `[pause]` and `[long pause]` stay its own). pieces() turns each into a mark the cutting keeps whole, so a pause ends its piece wherever it stands, between sentences or inside one, in a narration, by verse or in a dialog: one at the start of a turn waits before that speaker, one on its own line between paragraphs or turns waits after the piece before it, pauses written together add up, one before the first words is silence before the take, one at the very end stays (room for music after it); the engine reads up to it as a phrase of its own. `_join` makes an asked pause the pause heard, the quiet the trim keeps at both pieces' edges counted in, to the sample (`_quiet`), and writes the pause heard after every piece (`after`); a pause the text did not ask is joined as before, so an older take joined again stays bit for bit. `POST /reader/fix-gaps {id, gaps: {piece: seconds}, copy}`: in place it is a step of the take's history (Undo gives the take back bit for bit); with copy the run is copied, its pauses set, and its take lands in the Library beside the original as its child (request `parent` and `what: its pauses shaped`: the family tree shows it), the original and its run untouched and the copy's untouched pieces bit for bit the original's (the same gain). The room: «⏸ Pause» beside Check puts `[pause:1s]` at the cursor with its seconds selected to type over; the take's editor shows the pause heard after each piece as a number to the hundredth (past 60 s refused on the spot), and «Join with these pauses» and «Into a copy» once one changed; seven words in thirteen languages. The run counts its pauses. Verified: `lab/test_reader_pauses.py` (the tags in narration, verse and dialog; a run through the real worker with a made-up engine whose pieces keep a little quiet at their edges, each pause measured in the take within 10 ms of the asked one: 1.5 s before the first words, 0.6 s and 6 s after, a paragraph with no tag at its old 0.98 s; in place 2.25 s and Undo bit for bit; a copy with 0.85 s and 12 s whose request names its parent, the original's audio byte for byte as it was); `test_reader_fix.py`, `test_reader.py` and the other Reader tests pass; the page: `tools/claude-suite-reader-pauses.mjs` (kitchen, 11 checks against a stub on the live page, headless, no page error). The live lab reads it at its next restart.

**The guard on each piece: a voice or a tone after its last word cut, a tone under the words, a stall inside and a level far off said** (2335; the unified plan of 08.11.2026, the Reader's guards on every piece: «Whisper по CER, с перечиткой куска; высота тона; «ummm» и тоны на хвостах; громкость −16 LUFS»; 2266 and 2295 gave the first and the last, 2241 the pitch across gender). `lab/reader_tail.py`, after the ear and its re-reads, on each piece as kept; the ear (2295) now keeps each piece's last words with their times. After the text's last word, found among the last three heard (Whisper may write a hum as «Мм»), the speech ends at the first tenth of a second 35 dB under the piece's speech; what still sounds after it, 0.3 s or more, is a tail: voiced when pYIN finds a voice in 45 % of it (a hum, an «ммм», a syllable of no word, a word the engine added after the text), a tone when a steady narrow peak above 3 kHz holds 0.6 s within a bin (the Higgs dialog of 06.11 found at 7998 Hz, 21.7 dB over its neighbours), else noise (a breath: left). A voiced or tonal tail is cut where the speech ended, 20 ms faded, the reading as read kept beside it (`piece-NNN.tail.wav`); a tail joined to the last word with no silence between, running on 0.9 s past it (0.5 at first: 2345 says why), is said and never cut (Whisper's word end may fall inside the word); a text that ends in an engine's tag keeps its tail. A steady tone under the words, a silence of 1.2 s or more inside the speech (an engine's own pause asked excepted) and a piece 6 dB or more off the run's median level are said, for the editor to read that piece again. The run counts each (`tails`, `tones`, `holes`, `level_off`), the take's note says them, the run card says the tails cut and the pieces to listen to, and the editor marks each piece (✂ cut, ≋ joined, 〰 tone, ⋯ stall, ▲▼ level) with its reason in its tip; ten words in thirteen languages. A guard that could not look says so in the run and in the note, never a clean piece by silence. Verified: `lab/test_reader_tail.py` (a made-up voice of gliding pitch followed by a hum, a tone, a breath, nothing and a joined hum; a tone under its words; a stall; the pass over a run cutting two, saying the tone and the level, keeping the joined one, and saying a guard that failed); the room's suite as in 2334; its calibration on the Reader's own pieces of 07–10.11, heard as the room's ear hears them, in `MISC/claude-arc/reader/guards-20261110/`. The live lab reads it at its next restart.

**The speech chain in the Refiner: denoise, de-esser, speech EQ and speech loudness, the Reader's own nodes, and a pipeline of them** (2336; the unified plan of 08.11.2026, the Reader's links with the Studio: «Огранщик: речевая цепочка»; the protocol's §5: «шумодав, де-эссер, эквалайзер речи, громкость −16 LUFS… — Чтец»). Four steps of the Studio's own plugin (`lab/builtin_steps/ruach/speech_*.py`, their sound in `speech_core.py`), each `"realm": "reader"` as 2312 made it: the Refiner shows them for the Reader's takes and the lab refuses them on a song («Speech de-esser: only for the Reader's takes»). Speech denoise: ffmpeg's FFT denoiser (afftdn), its noise floor measured on the take's quietest stretches and followed as it moves, 3 to 30 dB (10). Speech de-esser: in the short-time spectrum, where the hiss band (4, 5 or 6 kHz to 11 kHz) rises over the voice's body (150 Hz to 4 kHz) past the threshold, and is loud enough to hear (within 30 dB of the loudest frame), only that band comes down, 4:1, 2 to 12 dB deep (6), at once and let go in 60 ms; the rest passes as it was; blocks of 2048 frames, so an hour's chapter is never held whole as a spectrum. Speech EQ: plenio_core's biquads by preset, Clear voice (80 Hz high-pass, −2 dB at 250 Hz, +2 dB at 3.5 kHz, +1.5 dB shelf at 10 kHz), Warm voice, Broadcast voice, Rumble only, the amount scaling every band but the high-pass. Speech loudness: plenio_core's master to −16 LUFS (podcasts) by default, −18, −19, −14 (video) or −23 (EBU R128), its true peak under the ceiling (−1 dBTP) and checked by an independent meter. Each comes back as a branch of the take with its measures and a summary. The pipeline «Narration: the speech chain» runs the four and Before and after (the plugin's own `pipelines`, so a release that leaves the steps home has no pipeline either: make-release and check-no-pro keep `speech_*.py` home with the Reader, as 2312 did the TTS Voice Upscaler). The words of the four steps and the pipeline in the Reader's catalog, thirteen languages, the presets named «Clear voice» and not «Clear» (the shared catalogs translate «Clear» as the button's «Очистить»). Verified: `lab/test_reader_speech.py` (a made-up voice at 48 kHz in stereo with a hiss under it and bursts of an «s»: the floor down 4 dB and more with the speech within 1 dB; only the hiss band down, by 3 dB and more where the «s» is, the voice's body within 0.2 dB and a word without an «s» within 0.002; the clear preset moving 250 Hz and 3.5 kHz the right way; −16 and −23 LUFS within 0.3 under their ceilings; the plugin loading four steps of the Reader's realm after the TTS Voice Upscaler and the pipeline valid); each step on a real take of 10.11 (210 s, Hebrew): the floor −83.3 → −87.3 dBFS in 20 s, the hiss lowered in 22.5 % of the frames by 2.6 dB on average in 8 s, the clear EQ in 4 s, −15.97 → −16.0 LUFS in 34 s; the live lab lists the four steps and the pipeline and refuses a step on a song. The Refiner's list of pipelines offers a pipeline of one realm's steps only for a take of that realm (`heresy-post.js`: the take's realm from /derived, as 2312 shows the realm's own steps; the one in hand always stays): on the live page the Reader's take «Слово Клода · HE» is offered the speech chain, the song «Я - Буратино v9.4.3» is not.

**The dataset doctor before a LoRA is trained** (2351; Timon's cherry ③ of 07.11.2026, from his #23, #145, #110, #149 and the beginner's #166 asking to be warned before a run: too few or too many songs, poor quality, MP3, a «wildly mixed» set; the unified plan of 08.11.2026, the Trainer: «Вишенка Тимона ③: доктор набора перед обучением LoRA»). `lab/dataset_doctor.py` looks at a raw folder track by track against the Studio's own guide (LORA-TRAINING.md): ffprobe (codec, rate, channels, length); the whole song decoded at 11025 Hz mono (silence at its ends under −45 dBFS, its loudness, its tempo by librosa's beat tracker); 20 s from its middle at its own rate, both channels: the spectrum's cliff (a fall of 25 dB within a kilohertz that stays down: an encoder's lowpass, 16–17 kHz for an MP3 of 128 kb/s even inside a WAV or a FLAC, where a dark recording only slopes) and samples at full scale. The report says: different songs (names with their versions, takes and numbers left out) and the length in all, against the guide (a style 20 or more, a voice 30 or a few hours, a language a hundred); versions of one song (three or more); the same file twice (its bytes); under 0:30, over 6:00; lossy sources; highs cut near 16 kHz, or below 20 kHz; below 44.1 kHz; mono; clipping (0.05 % of samples or more); silence over 3 s at an end; loudness from … to …, with those more than 6 dB from the median; the tempo's spread (a set called mixed when the middle eight tenths of its tempos, each folded into one octave, differ by more than a third and the raw ones by half: one odd track does not make a set mixed). At most 400 tracks, spread over the folder; parquet rows counted, not looked at; one folder at a time, in a thread at nice 15; kept in cache/train-doctor/NAME.json under the folder's signature (its files, sizes, times), looked at again only when it changes. GET /train/doctor?name=, POST /train/doctor {name, again}. In the Trainer's first step (`heresy-traindoc.js`, its own module: the Trainer's code untouched, it listens to the folder's pick) a panel under the folder's voice: a folder of up to 60 tracks is looked at when picked, a bigger one on «Look at the set»; how far it is; then a dot a finding (good, amber, red) with the names it is about, «Look again». It decides nothing: «The doctor says, the learner decides». 33 strings ×11; the guide ×12, a paragraph in 1 Material. Proven: `lab/test_dataset_doctor.py` on eleven tracks made by ffmpeg on a scratch kit (never datasets/): three versions of one song as one, a copy as the same file, the short one, the MP3 lossy and cut at 16.8 kHz with the FLAC made from it (and nothing else cut), the 22.05 kHz mono one, the hot one clipped and apart in loudness, 5 s of silence at a start, the kicked tracks at 120 BPM and the set not mixed, a second ask answered from the kept report, a changed folder not fresh: all ok, three times running. On his own `Fosforida_v2` (the guide's example: 42 tracks, versions of about a dozen songs): 11 different songs in 42 tracks, 4 h 49 min, eight songs with three versions or more (МАНИФЕСТ Крик ×8, ФИНАЛЬНЫЙ МАНИФЕСТ ×7, ВАЛЬКИРИЯ ×4…), 40 over 6:00, one cut at 18 kHz, one with 4.6 s of silence at its end, loudness −20.2 to −12.6 dBFS with none apart, tempo 86–185 BPM not called mixed. The page against the mock (the lab's answers stubbed): the panel under the voice, a small folder looked at by itself and how far, twelve findings with their names, Look again asking again, the panel in Russian, 0 page errors. The lab's routes are live since its restart at 19:38 (the song names' rule and the tempo's middle eight tenths after that, with its next restart).

**The seam of a song longer than the sound half's window: two even pieces, 6 s past their edge, a 4 s crossfade** (2352; measured 07.11.2026 on 25 takes of 21 days: the loudness 3.4 dB down in the quarter second after the edge (median), 2–3.5 dB down for the seconds after, a 1 dB fade before it, the same profile at random points of the same songs 0 dB; Timon's #183, mended in his 3.8.5; the unified plan of 08.11.2026: «Шов NAR в песнях длиннее ~400 с»). Found by replaying the same codes on the Arc (a kitchen build of the engine, `heresy/MISC/claude-arc/nar-seam/`): the first 8000 codes of three long songs fit one window, the reference; the same codes in two pieces of 4000 butted came out 1.5 dB under the reference in the first second after the edge and 1.45 in the next two (the lows −1.6, the air −2.7), one song −3.0; a short tail as the Studio made it (7000 + 1000) 1.8 dB under in the first second and 1.4–1.9 dB for the next twelve (its lows −2.9): a short window comes out quieter all through. Joined over margins: 150 frames with a crossfade of 50 either side gave −0.74 and −0.84 dB in the first three seconds, back to the windows' own −0.3 within five (75/25 and 250/100 no better); the overlap kept front-loaded (6850 + 1150) still left its tail −1.3 dB at 3–10 s, so the even pieces are half the cure. On the four whole long songs without a LoRA (415.8–456.7 s), the new seam against the old butt join with the same codes, seeds and decoder: over the old second piece +0.65 dB (+1.74 in its first 3 s), the lows +0.75, the air above 8 kHz +1.80 (+4.65 on «Ночная гостья у камина»); in the five seconds after the old edge the new version stands about 2 dB higher; at the new seam, mid-song, it follows the old within 0.4–0.8 dB; before it −0.46 dB (each window hears half the song); the windows agree at cos 0.84–0.91 over their 12 s of overlap; the sound half 13.6 % faster (two windows of 5,500 frames cost less attention than 9,400 and 1,600). The Studio's own engine as built tonight (SYCL) gave the kitchen's bytes: a minute in one window md5-identical to before, a long song identical to the kitchen's new seam. Now the pieces are even (the window the bigger of two, never a short tail) and each window hears 150 frames (6 s) past an inner edge, so neither end of a window falls near the edge; the two meet in complementary half-cosines 50 frames (2 s) either side of it, in their latents, from the same noise: the ladder's join (1768) on one edge. The first window is sealed past its piece as before (no prefill); the log says the pieces, the windows and how the two agree where they overlap (the cosine of their latents, their sizes). **The live spectrum follows whatever the player plays, and reaches 100 px further into each side** (2357; Viktor 11.11.2026: «Та живая волна спектральная, которую добавили ночью, а увидел её всего лишь на одном треке. После выхода из сравнителя её также нет в плеере. И можно расширить её по бокам на 100 пикселов с каждой стороны.»). Why 2354 lived on one take only, measured headless (Chrome 148 on the Forge, and his own Chrome 154 on the laptop): when the element moves to another source, its captureStream() stream keeps the old source's track «live» and silent and adds the new source's track after it (in 154, after a new src: two live tracks, the first at a peak of 0.000, the second 0.366); at the element's own end Chrome ends and removes its tracks and the stream goes inactive. 2354 listened to the first live track, so from the second take on it heard the first take's mute one (a click in the list, Next, the compare window handing its take back: each a new source), and after an end with the same source again (Repeat one) it found none live; only a natural end into the next take (Play on) happened to work. Now (`heresy-livespec.js`): the newest live track is the sound, the stream's addtrack moves it there, the tracks gone by are taken out of the stream and stopped (one live track at a time, never a pile), and where none is live with the element's metadata in, the element is captured anew; one capture an element. It follows whatever the player plays: the footer's `<audio>` looked up at each event through the document's capturing listeners (a new element in its place is the player too), and the compare window's version while that window has the player's sound (it takes the playing take over, 2044, and plays its own on opening, 2092): app.js's one sound at a time (1476) now names the element starting (`ruach-sound`), the spectrum follows that version under the window's veil, lets its capture go when the window closes, and the footer playing again takes it back. Wider: from 12 px clear of the side groups to 100 px further into each (88 px under their things), clamped to the bar, still at z-index −1 and taking no pointer, the 48 px fade at the new ends: 614–1306 px at 1920 (2354: 714–1206), 614–1946 at 2560 (714–1846). How proven, headless and muted on the mock with the song-shaped test signal and no autoplay flag (one real click gives the page its activation), `tools/claude-livespec2-probe.mjs`, 76 checks on the kitchen's page and again on the built one: after every step the spectrum draws and moves (two frames 300 ms apart differ, a peak of 0.68–0.90), hears the element that plays and holds one live track of it: take A, Next (B), C, the compare window opened while C plays (C goes on there), another version there, closed (handed back), paused and played again by real clicks, the compare window opened with the footer paused (its version plays by itself), paused there and closed (nothing drawn, its capture let go), ▶ in the footer, Play on at a take's end, Repeat one at its end (the same source: captured anew), the Opus stream and back to the FLAC, a new take made here landing and playing by itself (Play new takes, as a Retake or a variation lands); at 1920 and 2560, by day and by night, the new span, the foot on the player's last pixel and the top under the wave as before, the fade, every control of the side groups over it what the pointer finds at its centre, real clicks on ☆ and «Play on click» there; 2354's checks again (pause, the Defaults switch letting every capture go, reduced motion, the one-row rooms, devicePixelRatio 2, the boost's graph path, Hebrew); 0 page errors. **The Arc's watchdog: a hung Intel Arc is reset by itself, the engine refuses new work meanwhile and the page says so** (2358; Viktor 11.11.2026: «Для Сторожа Arc дай мне команду для добавления в sudo.»). The B50 hangs about weekly (01.11 at 12:53, 10.11 at 21:38, the second with GuC 70.72.1 already loaded): a job times out, then a kernel-submitted job times out again and again with a GT reset each time, the Studio's next engine hangs loading its model, and only a PCI reset brings the card back, by his hand with sudo. A kitchen unit on the Forge, `claude-arc-watch` (heresy/MISC/claude-arc/watch/arc_watchdog.py), follows the kernel's journal for 0000:03:00.0 and the engine's: three kernel-submitted timeouts within a minute with a GT reset among them, or a song on the Arc silent five minutes while /hardware says busy (the longest silence inside a normal job since 02.11 was 39 s, the hung load of 10.11 1393 s), is a hang; a single «Timedout job … in yue-server» with its engine reset (28.10, 05.11) is a lost job on a living card and is not. On a hang it writes tmp/arc-reset.json, stops ruach-studio, runs `sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/arc-reset` (his root-owned script: the fixed device, no arguments, one sudoers line), starts the Studio and waits two minutes without a timeout after the card's new «Initialized xe»; the job that was in work is named in its log (watch/arc-watch.log) and never sent again. Thirty minutes of cooldown and three resets a day: a hang inside them, a reset that did not take, or no sudo rule holds the card for his hand, said loudly, and the hold ends by itself when the card comes back. The engine (yue-server.cpp, only an engine on SYCL): while the note is fresh, touched within ten minutes, POST /synth, /vae and /transcribe answer 503 «The Arc is being reset: nothing new is taken until it is back». The lab (lab.py): the strip above the player shows «The Arc is being reset» or «The Arc hung: it waits for a reset by hand» with its clock, the Server log says each stage once and «back» at the end, and a note older than ten minutes is not trusted and that is said. The three sentences in the twelve catalogs. Our own users of the Arc (transcription tests, SheetSage2 batches, probes and decodes) go through watch/arc-lock.sh: /tmp/claude-arc.lock, never beside a render of the engine on the Arc, never while the watchdog holds the card; an engine that does not answer is not idle.

How proven: the replay of the kernel's journal of 10.11 21:30 → 11.11 07:30 (1.43 million lines, 0.7 s) saw the hang at its line 122, 21:38:59, 16.3 s after its first bad line, and the hold's end at 07:19:50 after his reset at 07:17:36; the same rule over every xe line since 28.10 saw the two hangs and nothing else (01.11 at 12:53:18, 16.5 s after its first bad line); the engine's journal alone saw the hung load of 10.11 at 22:00:05, 306 s silent. The new engine refused live for three seconds while nothing rendered (400 before, 503 with the note, 400 after it went; the lab's row and its two lines). arc-lock.sh against a fake engine and note: free, rendering on the Arc, rendering on CUDA, note fresh, note stale, engine silent, the lock held past the wait. Both binaries built (SYCL 57 s, CUDA 46 s); the Studio and the lab reloaded when empty (09:52); the watchdog enabled at 10:01.

**Three transcribers where a score is written from a recording: SheetSage2 · bf16 angles (the covers' default), SheetSage2 · exact angles (the sheets so far), SheetSage2-Refined** (2359; Viktor 11.11.2026: «Захерачим три режима SheetSage2 для FULL и Instrumental?», and on the lead's advice «Пока что делай как советуешь там»: SheetSage2 with the bf16 angles it was trained with becomes the covers' default, a dataset keeps the transcriber its sheets were written by.)

2328 found that SheetSage2 learnt with MERT's rotary angles rounded to bfloat16 and kept the exact ones for SheetSage2 (`YUE2_SS2_ROPE_BF16=1` asked for the other) until Viktor's word; on the Ring the rounded angles kept the chords (0.81) and took the false meter changes from 82 to 8. Now both are there to choose, beside Refined.

The engine: `/transcribe` takes `transcriber=sheetsage2-bf16` or `sheetsage2-exact` beside `refined` (query or form field). One loaded SheetSage2 writes with either angles, chosen for the call and given back after (`pipeline_transcribe`'s `rope`); a request that names none, or plain `sheetsage2`, is written as the server was started (exact unless `YUE2_SS2_ROPE_BF16`), so every older caller gets the same bytes. The answer names the one that wrote it: `sheetsage2-bf16`, `sheetsage2` (exact angles), `sheetsage2-refined`.

The page: Musician → Cover or Remix → From a Recording has three toggles, **SheetSage2 · bf16 angles** (the default), **SheetSage2 · exact angles** and **SheetSage2-Refined**, kept per browser (`yue2.transcriber3`; a 2328 choice of Refined carries over, SheetSage2 having been its default rather than a choice). A take of the Library and a Direct take's «Write it from the sound» are transcribed with the same choice; the status names the transcriber by the engine's word, and the lab keeps it beside the score from the sound (`score-from-sound.json`'s `by`). The status lines with the transcriber's name are in the twelve catalogs now (2328's were English in every language).

The Trainer: **Transcriber** offers the three and follows the set picked: the transcriber its sheets were written by (`sheets_by` in the lab's list of sets, the most files deciding), SheetSage2 · bf16 angles for a set without sheets; it hides in Direct, which writes no sheets. A run that names none takes the set's own. The bf16 sheets are files of their own (`NNN_ruach.full.bf16.abc`), and `yue-transcribe` is told its angles for every sheet, never inheriting the lab's environment; every set on the Forge holds SheetSage2's exact sheets and keeps them.

SheetSage2-Refined is on the Studio's Hugging Face: `goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2` commit c330df34, `models/SheetSage2-Refined-F16.gguf` (scragnog's file byte for byte), `models/SheetSage2-Refined/LICENSE` (anime-song's, CC BY-NC 4.0) and `NOTICE.md` (anime-song, scragnog, m-a-p, link by link), its lines in the repository's README, MANIFEST.tsv, SHA256SUMS, LICENSE.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Into the download lists as an extra of the transcriber with the models tree (2330).

How proven: a test server of the new build on the CPU: no transcriber, plain `sheetsage2`, `sheetsage2-exact`, and a call right after a bf16 one wrote the same score byte for byte, and the same as `yue-transcribe` with `YUE2_SS2_ROPE_BF16=0`; `sheetsage2-bf16` twice the same, and the same as the CLI with `=1`; bf16 and exact differ. The lab's `test_transcribers_2359.py` (19 checks). `node --check`; check-i18n 24 of 25 (its one red, «зроблено» in uk and be, came with 2298).

Measured on the Forge: eight threads writing one 1 MB target 200 times each, read back after every write: no torn file, no part file left; a write into a folder that refuses says false and the target keeps «old»; an `AtomicFile` dropped unclosed leaves no target and no part; the rebuilt mp3-codec writes a real take's MP3 and WAV (2.70 MB and 32.4 MB) and, into a read-only folder, says «Cannot write» with nothing left there. Now, with a display, AppRun first starts `window.py` (Tk of the image's own Python, no new dependency) and waits up to ten seconds for it to be on screen, before the setup copies a byte: the window says what the Studio does (setting up, the models missing, fetching, starting, running, stopped or failed with the log's last lines), what exactly is missing (the backbone, the decoder: found anywhere under models/, m-a-p's decoder or our RS x3 v1, so the models' new tree changes nothing), whether there is a network (a TCP probe of huggingface.co every five seconds); the plan of the download (each file and its size) appears only once it could be read, since a plan read offline says «0 KB … nothing to download»; *Fetch the models* wakes only online and downloads only on its press (fetch-models.sh --yes, its lines in the window, a stop in the middle goes on where it stopped next time); when the Studio answers, *Open the Studio* opens the page, and closing the window (or *Stop and quit*) stops the engine, the lab and its door. Without a display, or with RUACH_NO_WINDOW=1, everything is as before in the terminal. The C library: `libc.sh` (run by 70-appimage.sh on the AppDir) copies the build image's own glibc 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04, with gcc 12's libstdc++ and libgcc_s, 14 libraries, 6.7 MB, its LGPL source named in .runtime/libc/README) and turns every ELF program of the image (Python, the engine's yue-*, ruach-muscriptor, ffmpeg, ffprobe) into a two-line sh wrapper that runs the program through that loader with `--library-path` and `--argv0` (the program itself renamed .NAME.glibc, the loader hard-linked beside it so /proc/self/exe names its folder, where ggml looks for its CUDA and CPU modules); nothing goes into the environment, so the system's own programs the Studio starts keep the system's glibc. A bare system without certificates where Debian or Fedora keep them gets certifi's bundle (SSL_CERT_FILE), measured: in debian:10 the plan said «offline» on a live network. Measured on the Forge with the 2.0.6.1 tree repacked (`76-appimage-offline.sh`: a bare container, `--network none`, uid 1000, an Xvfb of its own, the window found by the X server's tree from outside): debian:10 (glibc 2.28) a window in 0.8 s, still up after 20 s, *the models are missing*, offline, button asleep; centos:7 (glibc 2.17) a window in 0.7 s, and with the models the whole Studio up offline on 2.17 as well (running after 2 s, health, the page, the lab); ubuntu:20.04 (2.31) a window in 0.7 s; debian:10 with the Q8_0 backbone and the decoder linked in, offline: the window in 0.6 s, *running* after 2 s, health ok, the page 17.5 MB, the lab through the engine, the CPU backend; the window's Stop ended it all in 2 s; online in debian:10 the plan (3.2 GB, two files) in 3 s and the button awake; every wrapped program on centos:7's 2.17 (Python with ssl, numpy, onnxruntime, av, cryptography, c2pa and a child of `sys.executable`; ffmpeg; the engine; ruach-muscriptor; hf); on the Forge itself through FUSE the CUDA module still found beside the engine.
